sentences.zh: 李諤李諤，字士恢，趙郡人也。

translations.literal: Li E—Li E, courtesy name Shihui, was a native of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li E, styled Shihui, was a native of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 好學，解屬文。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to learning and adept at prose composition.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為中書舍人，有口辯，每接對陳使。

translations.literal: He served Qi as Secretariat Drafter; he had eloquence in debate and every time received and answered envoys from Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Northern Qi he served as a secretariat drafter. Eloquent in debate, he was regularly assigned to receive envoys from Chen.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊，拜天官都上士，諤見高祖有奇表，深自結納。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he was appointed Director Clerk of the Celestial Office; E saw that Gaozu had an extraordinary appearance and deeply attached himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, Li E was appointed director clerk in the Celestial Office. Seeing that Yang Jian had an extraordinary bearing, he cultivated a close bond with him.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，甚見親待，訪以得失。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor, he was greatly treated with intimacy and favor and was consulted on gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yang Jian became chancellor, Li E enjoyed his close confidence and was consulted on the merits and failings of policies.

sentences.zh: 于時兵革屢動，國用虛耗，諤上《重穀論》以諷焉。

translations.literal: At that time military campaigns were repeatedly launched and state revenues were drained; E submitted the "Treatise on Valuing Grain" to admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: War was being waged repeatedly and the treasury was depleted. Li E submitted his "Treatise on Valuing Grain" as a pointed admonition.

sentences.zh: 高祖深納之。

translations.literal: Gaozu deeply accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian took his advice to heart.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，曆比部、考功二曹侍郎，賜爵南和伯。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, he successively served as Vice Director in the Ministries of Revenue Review and Merit Evaluation, and was granted the title Earl of Nanhe.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Jian accepted the throne, Li E served in turn as vice director in the ministries of revenue review and of merit evaluation, and was enfeoffed as Earl of Nanhe.

sentences.zh: 諤性公方，明達世務，為時論所推。

translations.literal: E's nature was upright and square; he was clear and penetrating in worldly affairs, and was esteemed by contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Li E was upright by nature and shrewd in practical affairs; contemporaries held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 遷治書侍御史，上謂群臣曰：「朕昔為大司馬，每求外職，李諤陳十二策，苦勸不許，朕遂決意在內。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman-in-Attendance of the Imperial Library; the Emperor said to the assembled ministers: "When I was formerly Grand Marshal, I repeatedly sought an external post; Li E set forth twelve policies and earnestly admonished me not to permit it; I then resolved to remain at court.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to gentleman-attendant of the imperial library. The emperor told the assembled ministers, "When I was grand marshal I often sought a provincial appointment. Li E offered twelve arguments and pleaded with me to refuse; I decided to stay at court.

sentences.zh: 今此事業，諤之力也。

translations.literal: As for the enterprise of today, it is E's doing.
translations.idiomatic: What we have achieved today is largely Li E's doing.

sentences.zh: 」賜物二千段。

translations.literal: " He was granted two thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Li E was rewarded with two thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 諤見禮教凋敝，公卿薨亡，其愛妾侍婢，子孫輒嫁賣之，遂成風俗。

translations.literal: E saw that ritual teaching was in decay; when high officials died, their beloved concubines and serving maids—descendants immediately would marry them off or sell them, and this became custom.
translations.idiomatic: Li E saw ritual norms in decline: when ministers and nobles died, their heirs would routinely marry off or sell the deceased's concubines and maidservants, until this became common practice.

sentences.zh: 諤上書曰：「臣聞追遠慎終，民德歸厚，三年無改，方稱為孝。

translations.literal: E submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that honoring the distant and being careful at the end makes the people's virtue return to thickness; three years without change—that alone is called filial.
translations.idiomatic: Li E submitted a memorial: "I have heard that honoring the departed and observing funeral rites with due care deepen public virtue, and that three years without change in one's father's ways is what truly counts as filial piety.

sentences.zh: 如聞朝臣之內，有父祖亡沒，日月未久，子孫無賴，便分其妓妾，嫁賣取財。

translations.literal: As I have heard, among court ministers there are those whose fathers and grandfathers have died—not many days and months have passed—yet worthless descendants immediately divide up their singing-girl concubines, marry them off or sell them to obtain wealth.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that among court officials, when a father or grandfather has died and scarcely any time has passed, dissolute descendants divide up the household's concubines and either marry them off or sell them for profit.

sentences.zh: 有一於茲，實損風化。

translations.literal: If there is one such case, it truly damages customs and transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Even a single such case truly degrades public morals.

sentences.zh: 妾雖微賤，親承衣履，服斬三年，古今通式。

translations.literal: Although concubines are slight and lowly, they personally received clothing and shoes from the deceased; mourning with sackcloth for three years is the common formula of antiquity and the present.
translations.idiomatic: Concubines may be of low station, yet they served their lord in person; wearing mourning sackcloth for three years has been the universal rule in every age.

sentences.zh: 豈容遽褫縗弊，強傅鉛華，泣辭靈幾之前，送付他人之室。

translations.literal: How can it be tolerated to suddenly strip off coarse hemp and forcibly apply lead and rouge, weeping before the spirit table to take leave, then send them to another man's chamber?
translations.idiomatic: How can they be stripped at once of their mourning garb, forced to apply cosmetics, made to weep their farewells before the spirit tablet—and then delivered into another man's household?

sentences.zh: 凡在見者，猶致傷心，況乎人子，能堪斯忍？

translations.literal: All who witness it are still caused grief; how much more sons—can they bear this cruelty?
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who witnesses such a scene is moved to grief; how could a son endure such cruelty?

sentences.zh: 複有朝廷重臣，位望通貴，平生交舊，情若弟兄，及其亡沒，杳同行路，朝聞其死，夕規其妾，方便求娉，以得為限，無廉恥之心，棄友朋之義。

translations.literal: Moreover there are weighty ministers of the court, whose rank and prestige are thoroughly noble; lifelong friends and associates, affectionate as elder and younger brothers—when they die, they become as distant as fellow travelers on the road; in the morning they hear of the death, by evening they scheme for his concubines, seeking betrothal by any convenient means, with gaining them as the limit—no heart of integrity and shame, abandoning the righteousness of friendship.
translations.idiomatic: There are also great ministers of high rank who in life were close as brothers; when a friend dies they treat him like a stranger met on the road—hearing of his death in the morning and by evening plotting to take his concubines, scheming by any means to obtain them, devoid of shame and betraying the bonds of friendship.

sentences.zh: 且居家理治，可移於官，既不正私，何能贊務？

translations.literal: Moreover in managing the home one can transfer principles to office; if one does not rectify the private, how can one assist in affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Domestic conduct shapes public service; if a man cannot govern his private life with integrity, how can he assist in state affairs?

sentences.zh: 」上覽而嘉之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor read it and commended it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and approved it.

sentences.zh: 五品以上妻妾不得改醮，始於此也。

translations.literal: That wives and concubines of fifth rank and above must not remarry began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The rule forbidding remarriage by wives and concubines of officials fifth rank and above dates from this memorial.

sentences.zh: 諤又以屬文之家，體尚輕薄，遞相師效，流宕忘反，於是上書曰：

translations.literal: E also saw that among families of belletristic composition the style still favored frivolity; they successively took one another as teachers and imitated, drifting and forgetting to return—thereupon he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Li E also observed that literary families favored a frivolous style, each imitating the other until excess became the norm. He therefore submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞古先哲王之化民也，必變其視聽，防其嗜欲，塞其邪放之心，示以淳和之路。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when ancient sage kings transformed the people, they necessarily changed their seeing and hearing, guarded against their appetites and desires, blocked their depraved and unrestrained hearts, and showed them the path of purity and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: I understand that sage kings of antiquity governed the people by reshaping what they saw and heard, curbing their appetites, closing off depraved impulses, and guiding them toward simplicity and virtue.

sentences.zh: 五教六行為訓民之本，《詩》《書》《禮》《易》為道義之門。

translations.literal: The Five Teachings and Six Conducts are the root of instructing the people; the Odes, Documents, Rituals, and Changes are the gateway of the Way and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The five teachings and six conducts are the foundations of moral instruction; the Odes, Documents, Rites, and Changes are the gateways to the Way.

sentences.zh: 故能家複孝慈，人知禮讓，正俗調風，莫大於此。

translations.literal: Therefore families could again be filial and compassionate, people knew ritual and yielding; rectifying custom and harmonizing winds—nothing is greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: Only thus could households recover filial devotion, and people learn decorum and forbearance; nothing does more to set right the manners of an age.

sentences.zh: 其有上書獻賦，制誄鐫銘，皆以褒德序賢，明勳證理。

translations.literal: As for those who submit memorials and present rhapsodies, compose eulogies and inscribe steles—all use them to praise virtue and set forth worthies, clarify merit and verify principle.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials, rhapsodies, dirges, and inscriptions should all serve to praise virtue, celebrate worthy men, and attest to merit and reason.

sentences.zh: 苟非懲勸，義不徒然。

translations.literal: If not for warning and encouragement, the principle does not exist in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Unless they admonish or encourage, they serve no legitimate purpose.

sentences.zh: 降及後代，風教漸落。

translations.literal: Descending to later generations, customs and teaching gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages moral instruction steadily declined.

sentences.zh: 魏之三祖，更尚文詞，忽君人之大道，好雕蟲之小藝。

translations.literal: The three ancestors of Wei further esteemed literary diction; they neglected the great Way of lordship, and loved the small craft of "carving insects."
translations.idiomatic: The three Wei emperors exalted polished phrasing, neglecting the ruler's great duty while indulging in trivial literary ornament—the "carving of insects."

sentences.zh: 下之從上，有同影響，競騁文華，遂成風俗。

translations.literal: Below following above, it was like shadow and echo; competing to display literary splendor, it thereby became custom.
translations.idiomatic: As ever below follows above, subjects raced to display literary brilliance until it became the custom of the age.

sentences.zh: 江左齊、梁，其弊彌甚，貴賤賢愚，唯務吟詠。

translations.literal: East of the Yangtze in Qi and Liang, the abuse was yet more severe; noble and base, worthy and foolish—all devoted themselves solely to chanting and composing verses.
translations.idiomatic: Under the southern dynasties of Qi and Liang the abuse grew worse still: high and low, wise and foolish alike cared for nothing but verse.

sentences.zh: 遂複遺理存異，尋虛逐微，競一韻之奇，爭一字之巧。

translations.literal: Thereupon they again abandoned principle and preserved eccentricity; sought emptiness and pursued minutiae; competed for the marvel of a single rhyme, contended for the cleverness of a single character.
translations.idiomatic: Writers abandoned substance for novelty, chasing empty effects and minute refinements, vying over a single rhyme or the cleverness of a single word.

sentences.zh: 連篇累牘，不出月露之形，積案盈箱，唯是風雲之狀。

translations.literal: Connecting pages and piling documents—nothing beyond the forms of moon and dew; filling desks and overflowing boxes—only the shapes of wind and cloud.
translations.idiomatic: Their pages piled up, yet described nothing but moonlight and dew; their manuscripts filled chest after chest, yet depicted only wind and clouds.

sentences.zh: 世俗以此相高，朝廷據茲擢士。

translations.literal: The worldly custom took this as elevation; the court on this basis promoted scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Society prized such writing, and the court selected officials according to it.

sentences.zh: 祿利之路既開，愛尚之情愈篤。

translations.literal: Once the path of salary and profit was opened, the feeling of cherishing and esteeming grew ever more intense.
translations.idiomatic: Once literary skill became a route to salary and promotion, devotion to it only deepened.

sentences.zh: 於是閭裡童昏，貴遊總丱，未窺六甲，先制五言。

translations.literal: Thereupon in lanes and hamlets, foolish youths and noble wanderers with hair still in knots—before having glimpsed the six jia, first composed five-character verse.
translations.idiomatic: Village children and young nobles who had barely learned their letters were already composing five-character verse.

sentences.zh: 至如羲皇、舜、禹之典，伊、傅、周、孔之說，不復關心，何嘗入耳。

translations.literal: As for the canons of Fuxi, Shun, and Yu, the doctrines of Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius—they no longer concerned the heart; how could they ever enter the ear?
translations.idiomatic: The classics of Fuxi, Shun, and Yu, the teachings of Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius—they no longer held any interest, scarcely reaching their ears at all.

sentences.zh: 以傲誕為清虛，以緣情為勳績，指儒素為古拙，用詞賦為君子。

translations.literal: They took arrogance and absurdity as clarity and emptiness; took indulging emotion as merit and achievement; pointed to plain Confucian simplicity as antiquated clumsiness; used rhapsodies and fu as the mark of gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: They called arrogance clarity, sentimental indulgence achievement, plain Confucian learning old-fashioned, and literary rhapsody the mark of a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 故文筆日繁，其政日亂，良由棄大聖之軌模，構無用以為用也。

translations.literal: Therefore literary compositions daily proliferated and governance daily fell into disorder—truly because they abandoned the track and model of the great sages and constructed the useless as useful.
translations.idiomatic: Writings multiplied while governance declined—the inevitable result of abandoning the sages' model and treating useless ornament as substance.

sentences.zh: 損本逐末，流遍華壤，遞相師祖，久而愈扇。

translations.literal: Harming the root and pursuing the branch-tip, it flowed throughout the flowering land; successively taking one another as teachers and ancestors, over time it fanned ever more.
translations.idiomatic: Esteem for the trivial over the essential spread across the land, each generation imitating the last until the trend flared without limit.

sentences.zh: 及大隋受命，聖道聿興，屏黜輕浮，遏止華偽，自非懷經抱質，志道依仁，不得引預搢紳，參廁纓冕。

translations.literal: When Great Sui received the Mandate, the sage Way suddenly rose; frivolity was dismissed and eliminated, florid falsity was checked and stopped—unless one embraced the Classics and held to substance, resolved on the Way and relied on benevolence, one could not be brought into the gentry ranks or participate among officials bearing insignia.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui received Heaven's mandate the sage Way was revived: frivolity was cast aside and ornate pretense restrained. Only those steeped in the classics and devoted to the Way could enter the ranks of the gentry and hold official office.

sentences.zh: 開皇四年，普詔天下，公私之翰，並宜實錄。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaihuang, a universal edict went to all under Heaven: public and private writings—all should be solid record.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 4 an edict went forth that all writings, public and private, must be plain and factual.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，泗州刺史司馬幼之文表華豔，付所司治罪。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year, the memorial and tables of Sima Youzhi, Governor of Sizhou, were florid and gorgeous; he was handed over to the appropriate office for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: That September, Sima Youzhi, prefect of Si province, was punished because his memorials were excessively ornate.

sentences.zh: 自是公卿大臣，咸知正路，莫不鑽仰墳集，棄絕華綺，擇先王之令典，行大道於茲世。

translations.literal: From this time the high ministers and great officials all knew the correct path; none failed to drill into and look up to the mound-collections, abandoning and rejecting florid splendor, selecting the excellent statutes of former kings, practicing the great Way in this generation.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter ministers and high officials knew the right course: they turned to the classics, rejected ornate display, took up the precedents of former kings, and practiced the great Way in their own day.

sentences.zh: 如聞外州遠縣，仍鐘敝風，選吏舉人，未遵典則，至有宗黨稱孝，鄉曲歸仁，學必典謨，交不苟合，則擯落私門，不加收齒；

translations.literal: As I have heard, in outer prefectures and distant counties the old abuse still clangs; selecting clerks and recommending men—they do not follow the canonical rules; indeed there are cases where clan and faction members are called filial, village and lane men are praised for returning to benevolence, study necessarily follows the canons and plans, association is not casual joining—yet they are cast aside at private gates and not recruited;
translations.idiomatic: I hear that distant prefectures and counties still clung to the old abuse: in selecting officials they ignored proper standards. Men praised for filial piety and integrity, who studied the classics and kept honest company, were rejected at the gate;

sentences.zh: 其學不稽古，逐俗隨時，作輕薄之篇章，結朋黨而求譽，則選充吏職，舉送天朝。

translations.literal: Those whose learning does not investigate antiquity, follow custom and keep pace with the times, compose frivolous chapters, form faction cliques to seek renown—then they are chosen to fill clerk posts and recommended and sent to the heavenly court.
translations.idiomatic: yet those who shunned the classics, wrote frivolous verse, and curried favor through cliques were appointed to office and recommended to the capital.

sentences.zh: 蓋由縣令、刺史未行風教，猶挾私情，不存公道。

translations.literal: This is probably because magistrates and inspectors have not carried out customs teaching; they still harbor private feelings and do not preserve public fairness.
translations.idiomatic: The fault lies with magistrates and inspectors who fail to enforce moral instruction, favor private connections, and neglect the public good.

sentences.zh: 臣既忝憲司，職當糾察。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly holds the post in the Censorate; his duty is to investigate and inspect.
translations.idiomatic: As a member of the censorate, it is my duty to investigate such matters.

sentences.zh: 若聞風即劾，恐掛網者多，請勒諸司，普加搜訪，有如此者，具狀送台。

translations.literal: If upon hearing the wind one immediately impeaches, I fear many will be caught in the net; I request to order the various offices universally to add search and inquiry—where there are such cases, fully report and send to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Immediate prosecution of every case might ensnare too many; I ask that all offices be ordered to investigate and report offenders fully to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 諤又以當官者好自矜伐，複上奏曰：

translations.literal: E also saw that those holding office liked to boast and vaunt themselves; he again submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Li E also observed that officials tended to boast of their achievements and submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞舜戒禹雲：「汝惟不矜，天下莫與汝爭能；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Shun admonished Yu, saying: "You alone are without boasting—under Heaven none contends with you for ability;
translations.idiomatic: I recall Shun's admonition to Yu: "Only by not boasting will no one under Heaven contend with you for ability;

sentences.zh: 汝惟不伐，天下莫與汝爭功。

translations.literal: You alone are without vaunting—under Heaven none contends with you for merit."
translations.idiomatic: only by not claiming credit will no one contend with you for merit."

sentences.zh: 」言偃又雲：「事君數，斯辱矣，朋友數，斯疏矣。

translations.literal: " Yan Yan also said: "In serving the ruler, if frequent, this is disgrace; with friends, if frequent, this is estrangement."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yan also said, "To serve one's lord too often is disgraceful; to importune a friend too often breeds estrangement."

sentences.zh: 」此皆先哲之格言，後王之軌轍。

translations.literal: These are all maxim sayings of former sages—tracks and ruts for later kings.
translations.idiomatic: These are the maxims of the sages and the path for rulers to follow.

sentences.zh: 然則人臣之道，陳力濟時，雖勤比大禹，功如師望，亦不得厚自矜伐，上要君父。

translations.literal: Thus the Way of ministers: presenting strength and aiding the age—even if diligence matched Great Yu and merit like the Duke of Shao—one must not thickly boast and vaunt oneself, pressing demands on ruler and father.
translations.idiomatic: A minister's duty is to serve with all his strength; even were his diligence equal to Yu's and his merit to the Duke of Shao's, he must not boast extravagantly or impose on his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 況複功無足紀，勤不補過，而敢自陳勳績，輕幹聽覽！

translations.literal: How much more when merit is insufficient to record and diligence does not remedy faults—yet dare self-present merit and achievement, lightly interfering with what reaches the ear!
translations.idiomatic: How much worse when one's merit is negligible and one's efforts fail to remedy one's faults, yet one still proclaims one's achievements and presumptuously intrudes upon the emperor's attention!

sentences.zh: 世之喪道，極于周代，下無廉恥，上使之然。

translations.literal: The world's loss of the Way reached its extreme in the Zhou dynasty; below there was no integrity and shame—the above made it so.
translations.idiomatic: Moral collapse reached its worst under the Northern Zhou: integrity vanished below because the court encouraged it above.

sentences.zh: 用人唯信其口，取士不觀其行。

translations.literal: In employing men they only trusted their mouths; in selecting scholars they did not observe their conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were chosen for their words alone, without regard to conduct.

sentences.zh: 矜誇自大，便以幹濟蒙擢；

translations.literal: Those who boasted and were arrogant were then promoted by claiming capacity;
translations.idiomatic: Men who bragged loudly were promoted for their supposed competence;

sentences.zh: 謙恭靜退，多以恬默見遺。

translations.literal: Those modest, reverent, quiet, and retiring were mostly overlooked through their plain silence.
translations.idiomatic: while the modest and retiring were passed over in silence.

sentences.zh: 是以通表陳誠，先論己之功狀；

translations.literal: Therefore in submitting general memorials and stating sincerity, one first discussed one's own merit and condition;
translations.idiomatic: Memorials therefore began with self-praise,

sentences.zh: 承顏敷奏，亦道臣最用心。

translations.literal: Bearing the countenance and presenting reports, one also said "your servant was most devoted."
translations.idiomatic: and audience presentations likewise dwelt on the speaker's devoted service.

sentences.zh: 自衒自媒，都無慚恥之色；

translations.literal: Self-displaying and self-promoting—altogether without the color of shame;
translations.idiomatic: Officials displayed and promoted themselves without a trace of shame;

sentences.zh: 強幹橫請，唯以幹沒為能。

translations.literal: forcibly pressing and horizontally demanding—only taking encroachment and seizure as ability.
translations.idiomatic: pressing their demands and grasping for gain as if that were talent.

sentences.zh: 自隋受命，此風頓改，耕夫販婦，無不革心，況乃大臣，仍遵敝俗！

translations.literal: Since Sui received the Mandate, this wind suddenly changed; plowmen and peddling women—none failed to reform their hearts; how much more great ministers—yet they still follow the old abuse!
translations.idiomatic: Since Sui received the mandate this custom has changed sharply; even farmers and marketwomen have reformed—yet great ministers still cling to the old ways!

sentences.zh: 如聞刺史入京朝覲，乃有自陳勾檢之功，喧訴階墀之側，言辭不遜，高自稱譽，上黷冕旒，特為難恕，凡如此輩，具狀送台，明加罪黜，以懲風軌。

translations.literal: As I have heard, when inspectors enter the capital for court audience, some self-present their auditing achievements, clamoring and pleading beside the steps; their words are not deferential, they greatly praise themselves—the above is profaned, the imperial regalia particularly hard to forgive; all such persons—fully report and send to the Censorate, clearly add punishment and dismissal, to chastise custom and regulation.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that when prefects come to court for audience, some noisily proclaim their auditing achievements on the palace steps, speaking impertinently and praising themselves—a grave offence against the throne. Let all such men be reported to the censorate, punished, and dismissed as a warning to others.

sentences.zh: 上以諤前後所奏頒示天下，四海靡然向風，深革其弊。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered E's successive memorials promulgated to all under Heaven; within the four seas all turned toward the wind like grass; the abuse was deeply reformed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Li E's memorials promulgated throughout the realm; all the empire turned toward the new standard and deeply reformed its ways.

sentences.zh: 諤在職數年，務存大體，不尚嚴猛，由是無剛謇之譽，而潛有匡正多矣。

translations.literal: E served in his post for several years, striving to preserve the larger framework, not esteeming severity and harshness; thereby he had no reputation for stern integrity, yet secretly he had many corrections.
translations.idiomatic: Li E served several years in office, keeping to broad principles rather than harsh severity; he won no reputation as a fierce remonstrator, yet quietly corrected many abuses.

sentences.zh: 邳公蘇威以臨道店舍，乃求利之徒，事業汙雜，非敦本之義，遂奏高祖，約遣歸農，有願依舊者，所在州縣錄附市籍，仍撤毀舊店，並令遠道，限以時日。

translations.literal: Duke of Pi Su Wei considered roadside inns and lodges to be profit-seeking people; the enterprise was filthy and mixed—not the principle of honoring the root; he therefore memorialized Gaozu to roughly send them back to farming; those wishing to continue as before—the local prefectures and counties would register and attach them to market rolls, still demolish the old shops, and also order distant roads, limited by days and months.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Pi Su Wei argued that roadside inns served only profiteers and corrupted the economy; he memorialized Yang Jian to return innkeepers to farming. Those who wished to continue would be registered on market rolls, their old establishments demolished, and travelers along distant routes given a time limit to adapt.

sentences.zh: 正值冬寒，莫敢陳訴。

translations.literal: It happened to coincide with winter cold; none dared to state grievances.
translations.idiomatic: It was the depth of winter, and no one dared lodge a complaint.

sentences.zh: 諤因別使，見其如此，以為四民有業，各附所安，逆旅之與旗亭，自古非同一概，即附市籍，於理不可，且行旅之所托，豈容一朝而廢，徒為勞擾，於事非宜，遂專決之，並令依舊，使還詣闕，然後奏聞。

translations.literal: E, on separate mission, saw it thus; he considered that the four peoples have their occupations, each attached to where they are at ease; travelers' lodges and tavern pavilions—from antiquity are not one uniform category; to attach to market rolls is in principle not permissible; moreover what travelers rely upon—how can it be abolished in one morning? Merely causing labor and disturbance—in the affair it is not suitable; he thereupon specially decided it, all ordered to continue as before; the envoy returned to the palace, and only then reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Li E, traveling on other business, saw the hardship and judged that each of the four classes of people had its proper occupation, and that inns and taverns had never been treated alike; registering them on market rolls was unreasonable, and travelers' accommodations could not be abolished overnight without useless disruption. He decided on his own authority to restore the old arrangements, then reported his action after the envoy returned to court.

sentences.zh: 高祖善之曰：「體國之臣，當如此矣。

translations.literal: Gaozu approved, saying: "A minister who embodies the state ought to be like this."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian praised him, saying, "A minister who truly serves the state should act as Li E did."

sentences.zh: 」以年老，出拜通州刺史，甚有惠政，民夷悅服。

translations.literal: Because of old age, he went out and was appointed Inspector of Tong Province; he had very benevolent governance, and common people and tribes were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew old he was appointed prefect of Tong province, where his benevolent administration won the affection of both Han Chinese and tribal peoples.

sentences.zh: 後三歲，卒官，有子四人。

translations.literal: After three years he died in office; he had four sons.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he died in office, leaving four sons.

sentences.zh: 大體、大鈞，並官至尚書郎。

translations.literal: Dati and Dajun both reached the office of Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Dati and Dajun both rose to gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 世子大方襲爵，最有材品，大業初，判內史舍人。

translations.literal: The heir Dafang inherited the title; he had the most talent and character; at the beginning of Daye he was designated Inner Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Dafang inherited the title. The most capable of his sons, Dafang was appointed acting inner secretariat drafter at the start of the Daye era.

sentences.zh: 帝方欲任之，遇卒。

translations.literal: The Emperor was just about to employ him when he happened to die.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to grant him greater responsibility when he died.

sentences.zh: 鮑宏鮑宏，字潤身，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: Bao Hong—Bao Hong, courtesy name Runshen, was a native of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Hong, styled Runshen, was a native of Tan in Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 父機，以才學知名。

translations.literal: His father Ji was renowned for talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji was known for his learning and talent.

sentences.zh: 事梁，官至治書侍御史。

translations.literal: He served Liang and reached the office of Gentleman Attendant Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he rose to gentleman-attendant investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 宏七歲而孤，為兄泉之所愛育。

translations.literal: Hong at seven years was orphaned; he was lovingly raised by his elder brother Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Hong lost his father at seven and was lovingly raised by his elder brother Quan.

sentences.zh: 年十二，能屬文，嘗和湘東王繹詩，繹嗟賞不已，引為中記室，遷鎮南府諮議、尚書水部郎，轉通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At twelve years he could compose writing; he once matched verses with Prince Xiangdong Yi; Yi sighed in admiration without cease, brought him in as Central Recorder, transferred to Counselor of the Southern Garrison Office, Gentleman of the Water Bureau in the Secretariat, then turned to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he could already compose prose and verse; when he matched verses with Prince Xiangdong of the Xiao clan, Yi admired him greatly and made him central recorder. He went on to serve as counselor in the southern garrison office, gentleman in the secretariat's water bureau, and regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 江陵既平，歸於周。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified, he submitted to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Jiangling he entered Zhou service.

sentences.zh: 明帝甚禮之，引為麟趾殿學士。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming greatly honored him and brought him in as an Academician of the Qilin Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Zhou treated him with great honor and appointed him an academician of the Qilin Hall.

sentences.zh: 累遷遂伯下大夫，與杜子暉聘于陳，謀伐齊也。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of the Sui Earl's domain; with Du Zihui he went on embassy to Chen to plot attacking Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand master under Earl Sui and was sent with Du Zihui on embassy to Chen to arrange a joint attack on Qi.

sentences.zh: 陳遂出兵江北以侵齊。

translations.literal: Chen thereupon sent troops north of the Yangtze to invade Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen duly sent troops north of the Yangtze to strike at Qi.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問巨集取齊之策，巨集對雲：「我強齊弱，勢不相侔。

translations.literal: The Emperor once asked Hong about the strategy for taking Qi; Hong replied saying: "We are strong, Qi is weak—the momentum is not comparable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked Hong for a plan to conquer Qi. Hong replied, "We are strong and Qi is weak; the two are not comparable in power.

sentences.zh: 齊主昵近小人，政刑日紊，至尊仁惠慈恕，法令嚴明。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler dotes on and draws near petty men; governance and punishments daily become tangled; Your Majesty is benevolent, kind, and forgiving, while laws and decrees are strict and clear.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler favors petty men, and his government grows daily more corrupt, whereas Your Majesty is benevolent and merciful and your laws are strict and clear.

sentences.zh: 事等建瓴，何憂不克。

translations.literal: The matter is like pitching a tile from a height—why worry about not conquering?
translations.idiomatic: Victory would be as easy as pouring water from a high roof—why doubt success?

sentences.zh: 但先皇往日出師洛陽，彼有其備，每不克捷。

translations.literal: But when the former emperor in past days sent out the army to Luoyang, they had their preparations, and each time success was not achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the former emperor marched on Luoyang, Qi was prepared each time and our forces failed to win.

sentences.zh: 如臣計者，進兵汾、潞，直掩晉陽，出其不虞，以為上策。

translations.literal: According to your servant's plan, advance troops through Fen and Lu, strike straight at Jinyang, catch them unawares—this is the superior strategy.
translations.idiomatic: In my view the best course is to advance through Fen and Lu and strike directly at Jinyang before Qi expects it.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 及定山東，除少禦正，賜爵平遙縣伯，邑六百戶，加上儀同。

translations.literal: When Shandong was settled, he was appointed Junior Director of the Imperial Household, granted the title Earl of Pingyao County with a fief of six hundred households, and given the additional rank of Pillar of State Equivalence.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Shandong he was appointed junior director of the imperial household, enfeoffed as Earl of Pingyao with six hundred households, and granted supernumerary pillar-of-state equivalence.

sentences.zh: 高祖作相，奉使山南。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, he was sent on mission to south of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian served as chancellor, Hong was dispatched on mission south of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 會王謙舉兵于蜀，路次潼州，為謙將達奚期所執，逼送成都，竟不屈節。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Qian raised troops in Shu; on the road passing Tong Province, he was seized by Qian's general Daxi Qi, compelled and sent to Chengdu—ultimately he did not bend his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Qian rebelled in Shu, Hong was seized en route at Tong province by Qian's general Daxi Qi and taken to Chengdu, yet he never yielded.

sentences.zh: 謙敗之後，馳傳入京，高祖嘉之，賜以金帶。

translations.literal: After Qian's defeat, he raced post-horses into the capital; Gaozu commended him and granted him a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: After Qian's defeat he rode post-horses to the capital; Yang Jian praised his fortitude and rewarded him with a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，加開府，除利州刺史，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication of the throne, (Hong) was additionally granted the office of Grand General, appointed Governor of Lizhou, and advanced in rank to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne, Hong was made grand general, appointed governor of Lizhou, and raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 轉邛州刺史，秩滿還京。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Qiongzhou; when his term expired he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Qiongzhou and, when his term ended, returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時有尉義臣者，其父崇不從尉迥，後複與突厥戰死，上嘉之，將賜姓為金氏。

translations.literal: At this time there was one Wei Yichen, whose father Chong had refused to follow Yu Chi Yong and later again died in battle with the Turks; the emperor commended this and was about to grant the surname Jin.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was a man named Wei Yichen whose father Chong had refused to join Yu Chi Yong and later died fighting the Turks. The emperor wished to honor this by granting the family the surname Jin.

sentences.zh: 訪及群下，宏對曰：「昔項伯不同項羽，漢高賜姓劉氏，秦真父能死難，魏武賜姓曹氏。

translations.literal: The emperor consulted his officials below, and Hong replied: "In olden times Xiang Bo did not follow Xiang Yu, and Emperor Gaozu of Han granted the surname Liu; Qin Zhen's father could die for the cause, and Emperor Wu of Wei granted the surname Cao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his court for advice. Hong answered: "Long ago Xiang Bo refused to follow Xiang Yu, and the founder of Han gave him the surname Liu. Qin Zhen's father died in service, and Cao Cao gave that line the surname Cao.

sentences.zh: 如臣愚見，請賜以皇族。

translations.literal: In this subject's humble view, I ask that he be granted the imperial clan surname.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble opinion, he should be given the imperial surname instead.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「善。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu said: "Good.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Wen said, "Well said.

sentences.zh: 」因賜義臣姓為楊氏。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he granted Yichen the surname Yang.
translations.idiomatic: " He then granted Yichen the surname Yang.

sentences.zh: 後授均州刺史，以目疾免，卒于家，時年九十六。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Junzhou; he was dismissed because of eye disease and died at home at the age of ninety-six.
translations.idiomatic: Later appointed governor of Junzhou, he was dismissed for failing eyesight and died at home at ninety-six.

sentences.zh: 初，周武帝敕宏修《皇室譜》一部，分為《帝緒》、《疏屬》、《賜姓》三篇。

translations.literal: Initially, Emperor Wu of Zhou ordered Hong to compile an Imperial Clan Genealogy in one fascicle, divided into three parts: Imperial Lines, Collateral Kin, and Granted Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Wu of Zhou had ordered Hong to compile an imperial genealogy in one volume, divided into three sections: imperial lines, collateral kin, and granted surnames.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in ten fascicles circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings, ten fascicles in all, circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 裴政裴政，字德表，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Zheng—Pei Zheng, styled Debiao, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zheng, styled Debiao, came from Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 高祖壽孫，從宋武帝徙家于壽陽，曆前軍長史、廬江太守。

translations.literal: Shou, a descendant of the founding ancestor, following Emperor Wu of Song, moved the family to Shouyang, and served as Chief Clerk of the Forward Army and Administrator of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: An early forebear named Shou, a descendant of the clan founder, had moved with Emperor Wu of Song to Shouyang and served as chief clerk of the forward army and administrator of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 祖邃，梁侍中、左衛將軍、豫州大都督。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sui was Attendant-in-Chief, General of the Left Guard, and Grand Governor of Yuzhou under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sui had been Liang's attendant-in-chief, general of the left guard, and grand governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父之禮，廷尉卿。

translations.literal: His father Zhili was Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhili was commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 政幼明敏，博聞強記，達于時政，為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Zheng was clever and sharp from youth, broad in learning and strong in memory, versed in affairs of the age, and praised by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Zheng was quick and bright, widely read with a formidable memory, and well versed in public affairs; his contemporaries praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 年十五，辟邵陵王府法曹參軍事，轉起部郎、枝江令。

translations.literal: At fifteen he was summoned as Legal Bureau Attendant of the Prince of Shaoling's household, then transferred to Gentleman of the Ministry of Works and Magistrate of Zhijiang.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he entered the Prince of Shaoling's household as a legal bureau attendant, then became a gentleman of the ministry of works and magistrate of Zhijiang.

sentences.zh: 湘東王之臨荊州也，召為宣惠府記室，尋除通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Xiangdong took up post in Jingzhou, he was summoned as Recorder of the Xuanhui Palace, and soon removed to be Direct Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Xiangdong went to Jingzhou, Zheng was summoned as recorder of the Xuanhui palace and soon made direct attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 侯景作亂，加壯武將軍，帥師隨建甯侯王琳進討之。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, he was given the additional title General of Robust Martiality and led troops following the Marquis of Jianning Wang Lin to advance and attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Zheng was made general of robust martiality and led troops under the Marquis of Jianning, Wang Lin, to attack him.

sentences.zh: 擒賊率宋子仙，獻於荊州。

translations.literal: He captured the bandit commander Song Zixian and presented him at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the rebel commander Song Zixian and brought him to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及平侯景，先鋒入建鄴，以軍功連最封夷陵侯。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, as vanguard entering Jiankang, for successive top military merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was defeated, Zheng entered Jiankang at the head of the army and, for repeated outstanding service, was enfeoffed as marquis of Yiling.

sentences.zh: 征授給事黃門侍郎，複帥師副王琳拒蕭紀，破之於硤口。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate, he again led troops as Wang Lin's deputy to resist Xiao Ji and defeated him at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court as attendant-in-ordinary of the yellow gate, he again took command under Wang Lin, defeated Xiao Ji at Xiakou, and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 加平越中郎將、鎮南府長史。

translations.literal: Given the additional titles General Who Pacifies the South and Chief Clerk of the Pacify-the-South Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made general who pacifies the south and chief clerk of the southern headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及周師圍荊州，琳自桂州來赴難，次於長沙。

translations.literal: When Zhou troops besieged Jingzhou, Lin came from Guizhou to the rescue and halted at Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Zhou forces besieged Jingzhou, Wang Lin marched from Guizhou to relieve the city and stopped at Changsha.

sentences.zh: 政請從間道先報元帝。

translations.literal: Zheng requested to take a bypath first to report to Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng asked to go by a hidden route first and report to Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 至百里洲，為周人所獲，蕭詧謂政曰：「我武皇帝之孫也，不可為爾君乎？

translations.literal: Reaching Baili Isle, he was captured by Zhou men. Xiao Cha said to Zheng: "I am a grandson of Emperor Wu—can I not be your lord?
translations.idiomatic: At Baili Isle he was seized by Zhou troops. Xiao Cha said to him, "I am a grandson of Emperor Wu of Liang. Cannot I be your sovereign?

sentences.zh: 爾亦何煩殉身于七父？

translations.literal: Why must you trouble yourself to die for your seventh uncle?
translations.idiomatic: Why should you throw your life away for your seventh uncle?

sentences.zh: 若從我計，則貴及子孫；

translations.literal: If you follow my plan, then honor will reach your descendants;
translations.idiomatic: If you heed me, honor will come to you and your children;

sentences.zh: 如或不然，分腰領矣。

translations.literal: if not, you will be parted at the waist and neck.
translations.idiomatic: if not, I will have you cut in two.

sentences.zh: 」政詭曰：「唯命。

translations.literal: " Zheng deceptively said: "Your command alone.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng pretended to agree. "As you command.

sentences.zh: 」詧鎖之，送至城下，使謂元帝曰：「王僧辯聞台城被圍，已自為帝。

translations.literal: " Cha locked him and sent him to the foot of the wall, making him tell Emperor Yuan: "Wang Sengbian, hearing that Taicheng is besieged, has already made himself emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " Cha had him bound and brought to the city wall, ordering him to tell Emperor Yuan, "Wang Sengbian, learning that the capital is besieged, has already declared himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 王琳孤弱，不復能來。

translations.literal: Wang Lin is isolated and weak and can no longer come."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin is alone and powerless and cannot come to your aid."

sentences.zh: 」政許之。

translations.literal: Zheng agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng assented.

sentences.zh: 既而告城中曰：「援兵大至，各思自勉。

translations.literal: Then he told those in the city: "Relief troops have arrived in great force—each of you should steel yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: But then he shouted to the city, "Reinforcements are near! Hold firm!

sentences.zh: 吾以間使被擒，當以碎身報國。

translations.literal: I was captured as a secret messenger; I shall repay the state with my crushed body."
translations.idiomatic: I was taken while carrying dispatches, and I will give my broken body for the realm."

sentences.zh: 」監者擊其口，終不易辭。

translations.literal: The guards struck his mouth, but in the end he did not change his words.
translations.idiomatic: His guards beat his mouth, yet he would not take back a word.

sentences.zh: 詧怒，命趣行戮。

translations.literal: Cha in anger ordered him hurried to execution.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Cha ordered him executed at once.

sentences.zh: 蔡大業諫曰：「此民望也。

translations.literal: Cai Daye remonstrated: "This man is the people's hope.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Daye urged him: "This man commands the people's respect.

sentences.zh: 若殺之，則荊州不可下矣。

translations.literal: If you kill him, Jingzhou cannot be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Kill him, and you will never take Jingzhou."

sentences.zh: 」因得釋。

translations.literal: Thereby he was released.
translations.idiomatic: On that advice, Zheng was spared.

sentences.zh: 會江陵陷，與城中朝士俱送于京師。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, together with court officials in the city he was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, he was sent to the Zhou capital along with the officials inside the city.

sentences.zh: 周文帝聞其忠，授員外散騎侍郎，引事相府。

translations.literal: Zhou Wendi heard of his loyalty and appointed him Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, drawing him into service at the Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wendi, hearing of his loyalty, made him supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and brought him into the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 命與盧辯依《周禮》建六卿，設公卿大夫士，並撰次朝儀，車服器用，多遵古禮，革漢、魏之法，事並施行。

translations.literal: He was ordered with Lu Bian to establish the Six Ministers according to the Rites of Zhou, set up ranks of duke, minister, grandee, and serviceman, and also compile court ceremony, chariots, robes, and implements—mostly following ancient rites, reforming Han and Wei laws—all put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: He and Lu Bian were charged to reorganize government on the model of the Rites of Zhou: six ministries, ranks from duke down to serviceman, and new court ritual, carriages, dress, and regalia. Much followed ancient precedent and replaced Han and Wei usage, and the reforms were carried out.

sentences.zh: 尋授刑部下大夫，轉少司憲。

translations.literal: Soon appointed Grandee of the Ministry of Punishments, transferred to Junior Director of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grandee of the ministry of punishments, then junior director of justice.

sentences.zh: 政明習故事，又參定《周律》。

translations.literal: Zheng was clearly versed in precedent and also participated in compiling the Zhou Code.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng knew precedent thoroughly and helped draft the Zhou legal code.

sentences.zh: 能飲酒，至數鬥不亂。

translations.literal: He could drink wine—to several dou without disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He could drink several dou of wine without losing his composure.

sentences.zh: 簿案盈幾，剖決如流，用法寬平，無有冤濫。

translations.literal: Documents piled full on the desk; he judged as if flowing water, applying law with lenience and fairness, with no wrongful excess.
translations.idiomatic: Case files piled his desk, yet he decided them as swiftly as flowing water, applying the law with lenience and equity and without wrongful severity.

sentences.zh: 囚徒犯極刑者，乃許其妻子入獄就之，至冬，將行決，皆曰：「裴大夫致我于死，死無所恨。

translations.literal: For prisoners guilty of capital punishment, he even allowed their wives and children to enter the prison to visit them. Come winter, about to be executed, they all said: "Senior Grandee Pei brought us to death—we die with no regret.
translations.idiomatic: Even men condemned to death were allowed to receive their wives and children in prison. When winter came and execution drew near, they would say, "It was Senior Grandee Pei who brought us to this, and we die without resentment.

sentences.zh: 」其處法詳平如此。

translations.literal: His handling of law was thus thorough and fair.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the thoroughness and fairness of his justice.

sentences.zh: 又善鐘律，嘗與長孫紹遠論樂，語在《音律志》。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in bells and pitch. Once he debated music with Zhangsun Shaoyuan; the account is in the Treatise on Pitch and Mode.
translations.idiomatic: He was also learned in bells and pitch standards and once debated music with Zhangsun Shaoyuan; that exchange is recorded in the Treatise on Pitch and Mode.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，以忤旨免職。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuan, for offending the imperial will he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he lost his post for speaking against the throne.

sentences.zh: 高祖攝政，召複本官。

translations.literal: When Gaozu held the reins of government, he was recalled to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took power as regent, Zheng was restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，轉率更令，加位上儀司三司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang, transferred to Director of Regulators, with additional rank Superior Chief of Protocol of the Third Order.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang he became director of regulators and was given the additional rank of superior chief of protocol of the third order.

sentences.zh: 詔與蘇威等修定律令。

translations.literal: Edicted to join Su Wei and others in revising laws and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: An edict put him with Su Wei and others to revise the laws and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 政采魏、晉刑典，下至齊、梁，沿革輕重，取其折衷。

translations.literal: Zheng drew on Wei and Jin penal codes down to Qi and Liang, tracing changes in severity and taking a balanced mean.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng drew on penal codes from Wei and Jin down through Qi and Liang, weighing how punishments had changed in severity and striking a balanced middle course.

sentences.zh: 同撰著者十有餘人，凡疑滯不通，皆取決於政。

translations.literal: Co-authors numbered over ten; wherever doubts stalled and would not pass, all were decided by Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten men worked on the project, but whenever a point stalled in dispute, Zheng's judgment settled it.

sentences.zh: 進位散騎常侍，轉左庶子，多所匡正，見稱純愨。

translations.literal: Advanced to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, transferred to Left Subordinate of the Crown Prince; he offered much correction and was praised as pure and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to regular attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and made left subordinate of the crown prince, he corrected many errors and was praised for plain, honest service.

sentences.zh: 東宮凡有大事，皆以委之。

translations.literal: For all major affairs of the Eastern Palace, everything was entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: All weighty matters of the crown prince's household were placed in his hands.

sentences.zh: 右庶子劉榮，性甚專固。

translations.literal: The Right Subordinate Liu Rong was by nature very obstinate and fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The right subordinate, Liu Rong, was stubborn by nature.

sentences.zh: 時武職交番，通事舍人趙元愷作辭見帳，未及成。

translations.literal: At the time military officers were rotating guard duty; Communication Attendant Zhao Yuankai was composing a memorial-account for audience but had not finished.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers were then rotating palace guard duty, and communication attendant Zhao Yuankai was drafting the written roster for the audience report but had not finished it.

sentences.zh: 太子有旨，再三催促，榮語元愷雲：「但爾口奏，不須造帳。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince had an order, repeatedly urging; Rong told Yuankai: "Just report orally—no need to make an account.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince pressed for the report again and again. Rong told Yuankai, "Just speak it aloud. There is no need to prepare the written roster.

sentences.zh: 」及奏，太子問曰：「名帳安在？

translations.literal: " When he presented the report, the Crown Prince asked: "Where is the name-account?
translations.idiomatic: " When the report was given, the crown prince asked, "Where is the name roster?

sentences.zh: 」元愷曰：「稟承劉榮，不聽造帳。

translations.literal: " Yuankai said: "Following Liu Rong's instruction, I was not allowed to make the account.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuankai answered, "Liu Rong told me not to prepare one.

sentences.zh: 」太子即以詰榮，榮便拒諱，雲「無此語」。

translations.literal: " The Crown Prince immediately questioned Rong; Rong then denied it, saying "There was no such statement."
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince confronted Rong, who denied it outright, claiming he had never said such a thing.

sentences.zh: 太子付政推問。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince entrusted the matter to Zheng for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince handed the case to Zheng for inquiry.

sentences.zh: 未及奏狀，有附榮者先言于太子曰：「政欲陷榮，推事不實。

translations.literal: Before the report could be submitted, one who sided with Rong spoke first to the Crown Prince: "Zheng wishes to entrap Rong—the investigation is not true.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zheng could submit his findings, a partisan of Rong told the crown prince, "Zheng is trying to frame Rong. His inquiry is false.

sentences.zh: 」太子召責之，政奏曰：「凡推事有兩，一察情，一據證，審其曲直，以定是非。

translations.literal: " The Crown Prince summoned and rebuked him; Zheng reported: "Generally in investigation there are two things: one, examining disposition; two, relying on evidence—scrutinize right and wrong to fix what is and is not.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince summoned and scolded him. Zheng replied, "Every inquiry rests on two things: reading the parties' conduct and weighing the evidence. One judges right and wrong and decides accordingly.

sentences.zh: 臣察劉榮，位高任重，縱令實語元愷，蓋是纖介之愆。

translations.literal: I examined Liu Rong—high in rank and heavy in responsibility; even if he truly spoke to Yuankai, it would be a trifling fault.
translations.idiomatic: Looking at Liu Rong's position, even if he did tell Yuankai what is alleged, it would be a minor lapse at most.

sentences.zh: 計理而論，不須隱諱。

translations.literal: Judged by reason, there is no need to conceal it.
translations.idiomatic: By any reasonable measure, he had no cause to deny it.

sentences.zh: 又察元愷受制于榮，豈敢以無端之言妄相點累。

translations.literal: Again I examined Yuankai—controlled by Rong, how would he dare with groundless words falsely implicate him?
translations.idiomatic: As for Yuankai, he was under Rong's authority. Would he dare invent a charge against him?

sentences.zh: 二人之情，理正相似。

translations.literal: The dispositions of the two men are, in reason, much alike.
translations.idiomatic: The conduct of both men points the same way.

sentences.zh: 元愷引左衛率崔茜等為證，茜等款狀悉與元愷符同。

translations.literal: Yuankai cited as witnesses Left Guard Commander Cui Qian and others; their confessions all matched Yuankai exactly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankai produced Left Guard Commander Cui Qian and others as witnesses, and their statements matched his in every detail.

sentences.zh: 察情既敵，須以證定。

translations.literal: With disposition on both sides equal, evidence must decide.
translations.idiomatic: Since the parties' accounts are evenly matched, the witnesses must decide the matter.

sentences.zh: 臣謂榮語元愷，事必非虛。

translations.literal: I say Rong spoke to Yuankai—the matter surely is not false.
translations.idiomatic: I conclude that Rong did speak to Yuankai, and the charge is not false.

sentences.zh: 」太子亦不罪榮，而稱政平直。

translations.literal: " The Crown Prince did not punish Rong either but praised Zheng as fair and straight.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince did not punish Rong, but praised Zheng for his evenhanded judgment.

sentences.zh: 政好面折人短，而退無後言。

translations.literal: Zheng liked to confront people's faults face to face, but in retreat had no words behind their backs.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was quick to rebuke a man to his face, yet never spoke ill of him afterward.

sentences.zh: 時雲定興數入侍太子，為奇服異器，進奉後宮，又緣女寵，來往無節。

translations.literal: At the time Yun Dingxing frequently entered attendance on the Crown Prince, wearing strange clothes and presenting exotic objects to the inner palace; also through favor with a daughter, his comings and goings lacked restraint.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yun Dingxing often attended the crown prince in outlandish dress, sent curios into the inner palace, and, trading on a daughter's favor, came and went without restraint.

sentences.zh: 政數切諫，太子不納。

translations.literal: Zheng repeatedly admonished sharply; the Crown Prince did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng admonished him again and again, but the crown prince would not listen.

sentences.zh: 政因謂定興曰：「公所為者，不合禮度。

translations.literal: Zheng therefore said to Dingxing: "What you do does not accord with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng finally told Dingxing, "Your conduct violates propriety.

sentences.zh: 又元妃暴薨，道路籍籍，此于太子非令名也。

translations.literal: Also the Primary Consort died suddenly; the roads were abuzz with rumor—this is no fine reputation for the Crown Prince."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's consort died suddenly, and scandal fills the streets. This does the crown prince no credit."

sentences.zh: 願公自引退，不然將及禍。

translations.literal: I hope you will withdraw of your own accord—otherwise calamity will reach you."
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw now, while you still can, or disaster will find you."

sentences.zh: 」定興怒，以告太子，太子益疏政，由是出為襄州總管。

translations.literal: Dingxing in anger told the Crown Prince; the Crown Prince grew more distant from Zheng, and thereby he was sent out as Governor-General of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxing, furious, complained to the crown prince. The prince grew colder toward Zheng, and Zheng was sent out as governor-general of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 妻子不之官，所受秩奉，散給僚吏。

translations.literal: His wife and children did not go to his post; the salary he received he distributed among his staff.
translations.idiomatic: His family did not accompany him to his post, and he gave away his salary to his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 民有犯罪者，陰悉知之，或竟歲不發，至再三犯，乃因都會時，於眾中召出，親案其罪，五人處死，流徙者甚眾，合境惶懾，令行禁止，小民蘇息，稱為神明。

translations.literal: When the people committed crimes, he secretly knew them all; sometimes he would not expose a case for a whole year, until after a third offense—then, at a public gathering, he would summon the offender before the crowd, personally examine the crime, execute five men, and banish many; the whole region was awed, orders were enforced and forbidden things ceased, the common people found relief, and they called him a spirit of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He kept quiet track of every crime in his jurisdiction. Often he would let a man go unpunished for a year, even two, until a third offense; then, at a public assembly, he would call the offender out before the crowd, hear the case himself, put five men to death, and exile many more. The whole region trembled; order held, litigation nearly ceased, and the people breathed easier, calling him a divine magistrate.

sentences.zh: 爾後不修囹圄，殆無爭訟。

translations.literal: Afterward he barely maintained prisons; scarcely any litigation.
translations.idiomatic: After that he scarcely needed his prisons, and lawsuits all but disappeared.

sentences.zh: 卒官，年八十九。

translations.literal: Died in office at eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 著《承聖降錄》十卷。

translations.literal: He authored Record of the Chengsheng Surrender in ten fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Record of the Chengsheng Surrender in ten fascicles.

sentences.zh: 及太子廢，高祖追憶之曰：「向遣裴政、劉行本在，共匡弼之，猶應不令至此。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was deposed, Gaozu recalled him and said: "If only Pei Zheng and Liu Xingben had been kept on to assist and correct together, he still should not have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince was deposed, Emperor Wen looked back and said, "If Pei Zheng and Liu Xingben had remained to guide him, things might never have come to this.

sentences.zh: 」子南金，仕至膳部郎。

translations.literal: " His son Nanjin served up to Gentleman of the Provisioners' Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: " His son Nanjin rose to gentleman of the provisioners' bureau.

sentences.zh: 柳莊柳莊，字思敬，河東解人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhuang—Liu Zhuang, styled Sijing, was a native of Jie in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhuang, styled Sijing, came from Jie in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖季遠，梁司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jiyuan was Attendant of the Eastern Department under the Liang Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jiyuan had been attendant of the eastern department under Liang's minister over the masses.

sentences.zh: 父遐，霍州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xia was Governor of Huozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xia was governor of Huozhou.

sentences.zh: 莊少有遠量，博覽墳籍，兼善辭令。

translations.literal: Zhuang from youth had far-reaching capacity, browsed broadly the classics, and was also skilled in rhetoric.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zhuang had breadth of mind, read widely in the classics, and was gifted in speech and writing.

sentences.zh: 濟陽蔡大寶有重名于江左，時為岳陽王蕭詧諮議，見莊便歎曰：「襄陽水鏡，複在於茲矣。

translations.literal: Cai Dabao of Jiyang had great renown in the lands east of the Yangtze; then serving as Adviser to the Prince of Yueyang Xiao Cha, seeing Zhuang he at once sighed: "The water mirror of Xiangyang exists here again.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Dabao of Jiyang was famed throughout the south. Serving as adviser to the Prince of Yueyang, Xiao Cha, he saw Zhuang and exclaimed, "The clear mirror of Xiangyang has appeared again.

sentences.zh: 」大寶遂以女妻之，俄而詧辟為參軍，轉法曹。

translations.literal: " Dabao thereupon gave him his daughter in marriage. Soon Cha summoned him as staff officer, transferred to Legal Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: " Dabao gave him his daughter in marriage. Soon afterward Xiao Cha summoned Zhuang as a staff officer and later made him head of the legal bureau.

sentences.zh: 及詧稱帝，還署中書舍人，曆給事黃門侍郎、吏部郎中、鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: When Cha declared himself emperor, he was again appointed Palace Attendant, then successively Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Chamberlain for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha declared himself emperor, Zhuang became palace attendant and later served in turn as attendant-in-ordinary of the yellow gate, director of the ministry of personnel, and chamberlain for dependencies.

sentences.zh: 及高祖輔政，蕭巋令莊奉書入關。

translations.literal: When Gaozu held the government, Xiao Kui ordered Zhuang to carry a letter through the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became regent, Xiao Kui sent Zhuang through the pass with a letter to him.

sentences.zh: 時三方構難，高祖懼巋有異志，及莊還，謂莊曰：「孤昔以開府從役江陵，深蒙梁主殊眷。

translations.literal: At the time the three regions were embroiled in strife; Gaozu feared Kui had divergent aims. When Zhuang returned, he said: "I once, as open prefect, followed service at Jiangling and received the Liang ruler's exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was then divided in three, and Yang Jian feared Xiao Kui might turn against him. When Zhuang returned, Yang Jian told him, "Long ago I served at Jiangling as an open prefect and received extraordinary kindness from the Liang ruler.

sentences.zh: 今主幼時艱，猥蒙顧托，中夜自省，實懷慚懼。

translations.literal: Now the ruler is young and times are hard; I have undeservedly received his trust and entrustment; in the deep night examining myself, I truly harbor shame and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Now the throne is held by a child in troubled times, and I have been undeservedly entrusted with power. At night, when I examine myself, I am filled with shame and dread.

sentences.zh: 梁主奕葉重光，委誠朝廷，而今已後，方見松筠之節。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler's line shines generation after generation, entrusting sincerity to the court—from now on you will see the steadfastness of pine and bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Liang has long stood in honor and has shown its loyalty to the court. Hereafter you will see that its integrity is as firm as pine and bamboo.

sentences.zh: 君還本國，幸申孤此意于梁主也。

translations.literal: Sir, returning to your state, I hope you will convey this unworthy one's meaning to the Liang ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When you return home, please convey this humble wish of mine to the Liang ruler.

sentences.zh: 」遂執莊手而別。

translations.literal: " With that he took Zhuang by the hand and parted.
translations.idiomatic: With that he took Zhuang by the hand and bid him farewell.

sentences.zh: 時梁之將帥鹹潛請興師，與尉迥等為連衡之勢，進可以盡節于周氏，退可以席捲山南。

translations.literal: At that time the Liang generals all secretly petitioned to raise troops, to form a united front with Wei Chidao and others—in advance they could exhaust their loyalty to the Zhou house; in retreat they could sweep through the lands south of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Liang commanders all secretly urged raising an army and joining Wei Chidao and others in a coalition: advancing, they could prove their loyalty to the Zhou; retreating, they could overrun the country south of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 唯巋疑為不可。

translations.literal: Only Xiao Kui doubted and considered it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xiao Kui was skeptical and thought it unwise.

sentences.zh: 會莊至自長安，具申高祖結托之意，遂言於巋曰：「昔袁紹、劉表、王淩、諸葛誕之徒，並一時之雄傑也。

translations.literal: When Zhuang arrived from Chang'an, he fully explained the Gaozu's entrustment, and then said to Xiao Kui: "In the past, Yuan Shao, Liu Biao, Wang Ling, Zhuge Dan, and their ilk were all heroes of their age.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuang returned from Chang'an, he fully relayed the Gaozu's pledge of trust, then said to Xiao Kui: "In former times Yuan Shao, Liu Biao, Wang Ling, Zhuge Dan, and men like them were all heroes of their generation.

sentences.zh: 及據要害之地，擁哮闞之群，功業莫建，而禍不旋踵者，良由魏武、晉氏挾天子，保京都，仗大義以為名，故能取威定霸。

translations.literal: When they held strategic positions and commanded fierce, arrogant hosts, yet built no lasting achievement while disaster followed hard on their heels, it was precisely because Cao Cao of Wei and the Jin clan held the Son of Heaven, guarded the capital, and relied on the banner of righteous cause—thus they could gather prestige and settle hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once they held vital ground and led fierce, unruly armies, none established lasting success while ruin overtook them without delay—because Cao Cao of Wei and the house of Jin held the Son of Heaven, protected the capital, and acted in the name of righteous authority, and so could win awe and fix their dominion.

sentences.zh: 今尉迥雖曰舊將，昏耄已甚，消難、王謙，常人之下者，非有匡合之才。

translations.literal: Now Wei Chidao may be called an old general, but he is already deeply senile; Xiaonan and Wang Qian are below ordinary men—they lack talent to unite and restore the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chidao may be an old commander, but he is already far gone in age; Xiaonan and Wang Qian are men beneath the common run and possess no gift for rallying the realm.

sentences.zh: 況山東、庸蜀從化日近，周室之恩未洽，在朝將相，多為身計，競效節于楊氏。

translations.literal: Moreover, Shandong and Yong-Shu grow daily nearer to submission; the Zhou house's grace has not yet fully reached them; ministers and generals at court mostly scheme for themselves, competing to give their loyalty to the Yang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Shandong and the Yong-Shu region draw closer to submission every day, while the Zhou court's favor has not yet won them over; many ministers and generals at court look to their own interests and vie to show loyalty to the Yang clan.

sentences.zh: 以臣料之，迥等終當覆滅，隋公必移周國。

translations.literal: In my judgment, Wei Chidao and his company will in the end be overthrown, and Duke of Sui will surely transfer Zhou's realm.
translations.idiomatic: By my reckoning, Wei Chidao and his allies will ultimately be destroyed, and the Duke of Sui is sure to supplant the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 未若保境息民，以觀其變。

translations.literal: Better to guard your borders, let the people rest, and watch how events unfold.
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold your territory, give the people peace, and wait to see how matters develop.

sentences.zh: 」巋深以為然，眾議遂止。

translations.literal: " Xiao Kui deeply agreed, and the collective deliberation ceased.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiao Kui was fully persuaded, and the assembly's plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 未幾，消難奔陳，迥及謙相次就戮，巋謂莊曰：「近者若從眾人之言，社稷已不守矣。

translations.literal: Before long, Xiaonan fled to Chen; Wei Chidao and Wang Qian were executed in succession. Xiao Kui said to Zhuang: "Had I lately followed the crowd's counsel, the altars of state would already be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xiaonan fled to Chen, and Wei Chidao and Wang Qian were put to death in turn. Xiao Kui said to Zhuang: "Had I recently heeded the others, the state would already be lost.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，莊又入朝，高祖深慰勉之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Zhuang again came to court; Gaozu deeply comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaozu took the throne, Zhuang again presented himself at court, and the Gaozu warmly comforted and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 及為晉王廣納妃于梁，莊因是往來四五反，前後賜物數千段。

translations.literal: When he took a princess from Liang for Prince Jin Guang's consort, Zhuang made four or five round trips on this account; he was given gifts totaling several thousand lengths of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When a bride was taken from Liang for Prince Jin of Guang, Zhuang traveled back and forth four or five times on the mission and was granted several thousand lengths of goods in all.

sentences.zh: 蕭琮嗣位，遷太府卿。

translations.literal: When Xiao Cong succeeded to the throne, Zhuang was promoted to Grand Steward of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cong succeeded to the throne, Zhuang was transferred to Grand Steward of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 及梁國廢，授開府儀同三司，尋除給事黃門侍郎，並賜以田宅。

translations.literal: When the Liang state was abolished, he was appointed Grand Master with Pomp equaling a third-rank office; soon after he was made Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and lands and houses were granted him as well.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang realm was abolished, he was given the title of Grand Master with Pomp equaling a third-rank office; soon afterward he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and was also granted fields and a residence.

sentences.zh: 莊明習舊章，雅達政事，凡所駁正，帝莫不稱善。

translations.literal: Zhuang was thoroughly versed in old statutes and elegantly skilled in administration; whatever he corrected in review, the Emperor invariably praised as good.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang knew the old regulations well and had a refined grasp of government; every correction he offered in review the Emperor praised without exception.

sentences.zh: 蘇威為納言，重莊器識，常奏帝雲：「江南人有學業者，多不習世務，習世務者，又無學業。

translations.literal: Su Wei served as Chief Censor; he valued Zhuang's capacity and insight and often memorialized the Emperor: "Among men of Jiangnan with scholarly learning, many do not understand affairs of the world; those who understand affairs of the world, in turn, have no scholarly learning.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, as Chief Censor, esteemed Zhuang's talent and judgment and often told the Emperor: "Among the learned men of Jiangnan, many are unversed in practical affairs; those versed in practical affairs, in turn, lack learning.

sentences.zh: 能兼之者，不過於柳莊。

translations.literal: One who combines both is none other than Liu Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The man who unites both qualities is none other than Liu Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 」高熲亦與莊甚厚。

translations.literal: " Gao Jiong was also very close with Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Jiong was also on very close terms with Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 莊與陳茂同官，不能降意，茂見上及朝臣多屬意于莊，心每不平，常謂莊為輕己。

translations.literal: Zhuang and Chen Mao held the same office, but Zhuang would not lower himself in deference; Mao saw that the Emperor and court ministers favored Zhuang, and his heart was always resentful—he often said Zhuang looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang and Chen Mao served in the same office, but Zhuang would not humble himself; Mao saw that the Emperor and the court favored Zhuang, and his heart was always uneasy—he often said Zhuang slighted him.

sentences.zh: 帝與茂有舊，曲被引召，數陳莊短。

translations.literal: The Emperor had old ties with Mao and repeatedly summoned him with special favor; Mao often cited Zhuang's faults.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had long-standing ties with Mao and repeatedly summoned him with special indulgence; Mao often listed Zhuang's faults.

sentences.zh: 經歷數載，譖醖頗行。

translations.literal: Several years passed, and slander took deep root.
translations.idiomatic: After several years, calumny had taken deep hold.

sentences.zh: 尚書省嘗奏犯罪人依法合流，而上處以大辟。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Affairs once memorialized that a criminal should by law be banished, but the Emperor sentenced him to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Affairs once reported that a convicted man should by law be exiled, but the Emperor ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 莊奏曰：「臣聞張釋之有言，法者天子所與天下共也。

translations.literal: Zhuang memorialized: "Your servant has heard Zhang Shizhi's saying: the law is what the Son of Heaven shares with all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang memorialized: "I have heard Zhang Shizhi's words: the law is what the Son of Heaven shares with all the world.

sentences.zh: 今法如是，更重之，是法不信于民心。

translations.literal: Now the law reads thus, yet it is made heavier—this means the law is not trusted in the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Now the statute says one thing, yet the sentence is made heavier—this means the law will not be trusted in the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 方今海內無事，正是示信之時，伏願陛下思釋之之言，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: At present the realm within the seas is at peace—this is precisely the time to display trustworthiness. I humbly wish Your Majesty would reflect on Shizhi's words; then all under Heaven would be greatly blessed.
translations.idiomatic: At present the realm is at peace—this is exactly the time to show good faith. I humbly beg Your Majesty to ponder Shizhi's counsel; then the empire would be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 」帝不從，由是忤旨。

translations.literal: " The Emperor did not agree; thereby Zhuang offended the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor would not heed him, and Zhuang thereby fell afoul of the throne.

sentences.zh: 俄屬尚藥進丸藥不稱旨，茂因密奏莊不親監臨，帝遂怒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, when the Office of Imperial Medicines presented pills that did not meet expectation, Mao secretly memorialized that Zhuang had not personally supervised—thereupon the Emperor grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, when the Office of Imperial Medicines presented pills that failed to please, Mao secretly reported that Zhuang had not personally overseen the matter, and the Emperor grew angry.

sentences.zh: 十一年，徐璒等反於江南，以行軍總管長史隨軍討之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Xu Zan and others rebelled in Jiangnan; Zhuang served as chief clerk to the campaign commander and accompanied the army to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Xu Zan and others rose in rebellion in Jiangnan; Zhuang served as chief clerk on the punitive campaign and marched with the army.

sentences.zh: 璒平，即授饒州刺史，甚有治名。

translations.literal: Once Xu Zan was pacified, Zhuang was immediately appointed governor of Raozhou, where he earned an excellent reputation for governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Zan was subdued, Zhuang was at once appointed governor of Raozhou, where he won a strong reputation for good administration.

sentences.zh: 後數載卒官，年六十二。

translations.literal: Several years later he died in office, at age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later he died in office, at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 源師源師，字踐言，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Shi—Yuan Shi, courtesy name Jianyan, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shi, courtesy name Jianyan, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父文宗，有重名于齊，開皇初，終於莒州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Wenzong enjoyed a great reputation in Qi; in the early Kaihuang era he died in office as governor of Juzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenzong had a great name in Qi; in the early Kaihuang reign he died in office as governor of Juzhou.

sentences.zh: 師早有聲望，起家司空府參軍事，稍遷尚書左外兵郎中，又攝祠部。

translations.literal: Shi had early fame; he began his career as a staff officer in the Office of the Minister of Works, gradually rose to Director in the Left Outer Bureau of Military Affairs in the Ministry of Affairs, and also acted head of the Sacrificial Rites section.
translations.idiomatic: Shi won early renown. He entered service as a staff officer in the Office of the Minister of Works, gradually rose to Director in the Left Outer Bureau of Military Affairs under the Ministry of Affairs, and also served concurrently as head of the Sacrificial Rites section.

sentences.zh: 後屬孟夏，以龍見請雩。

translations.literal: Later, during the first month of summer, when the Dragon constellation appeared, he requested the rain rite.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in the first month of summer, when the Azure Dragon star appeared, he requested the rain sacrifice.
