sentences.zh: 時高阿那肱為相，謂真龍出見，大驚喜，問龍所在，師整容報曰：「此是龍星初見，依禮當雩祭郊壇，非謂真龍別有所降。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Anaqi served as chancellor; thinking a real dragon had appeared, he was greatly astonished and delighted, and asked where the dragon was. Shi composed himself and replied: "This is the first appearance of the Azure Dragon star. According to ritual, one should perform the rain sacrifice at the suburban altar—it does not mean a real dragon has descended elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gao Anaqi was chancellor; believing a real dragon had appeared, he was greatly startled and delighted and asked where the dragon was. Shi composed himself and answered: "This is the first sighting of the Azure Dragon star. By ritual one should offer the rain sacrifice at the suburban altar—it does not mean an actual dragon has descended somewhere else.

sentences.zh: 」阿那肱忿然作色曰：「何乃幹知星宿！

translations.literal: " Anaqi flushed with anger and said: "How dare you meddle in knowledge of the stars!
translations.idiomatic: " Anaqi flushed with anger and said: "What business have you interfering in knowledge of the stars!

sentences.zh: 」祭竟不行。

translations.literal: " The sacrifice was ultimately not performed.
translations.idiomatic: " The sacrifice was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 師出而竊歎曰：「國家大事，在祀與戎。

translations.literal: Shi went out and sighed privately: "The great affairs of the state lie in sacrifice and war.
translations.idiomatic: Shi left and sighed to himself: "The great affairs of the state lie in sacrifice and arms.

sentences.zh: 禮既廢也，何能久乎？

translations.literal: Now rites are abandoned—how can it long endure?
translations.idiomatic: When ritual is cast aside, how can the state long endure?

sentences.zh: 齊亡無日矣。

translations.literal: Qi's fall is a matter of days.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's destruction is only a matter of time.

sentences.zh: 」七年，周武帝平齊，授司賦上士。

translations.literal: " In the seventh year, Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi; Shi was appointed a senior clerk in the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: " In the seventh year Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, and Shi was appointed a senior clerk in the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，除魏州長史，入為尚書考功侍郎，仍攝吏部。

translations.literal: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, Shi was made chief administrator of Weizhou; he entered court as Vice Director of the Evaluation Bureau in the Ministry of Affairs, and still acted head of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaozu received the abdication, Shi was made chief administrator of Weizhou; he then entered the capital as Vice Director of the Evaluation Bureau in the Ministry of Affairs and continued to serve concurrently as head of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 朝章國憲，多所參定。

translations.literal: He participated in drafting many court regulations and national statutes.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in drafting many court regulations and national laws.

sentences.zh: 十七年，曆尚書左右丞，以明幹著稱。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he served successively as left and right assistant ministers of the Ministry of Affairs, renowned for clarity and competence.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he served in turn as left and right assistant minister of the Ministry of Affairs, famed for clarity and efficiency.

sentences.zh: 時蜀王秀頗違法度，乃以師為益州總管司馬。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Shu Xiu frequently violated law and custom; Shi was therefore appointed chief administrator under the Grand Commander of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Xiu of Shu often transgressed law and custom, and Shi was therefore appointed chief administrator under the Grand Commander of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 俄而秀被征，秀恐京師有變，將謝病不行。

translations.literal: Soon Xiu was summoned; fearing change in the capital, he intended to plead illness and not go.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xiu was summoned to court; fearing trouble in the capital, he planned to plead illness and refuse to go.

sentences.zh: 師數勸之不可違命，秀作色曰：「此自我家事，何預卿也！

translations.literal: Shi repeatedly urged that he must not defy the command. Xiu changed color and said: "This is my own family matter—what business is it of yours!
translations.idiomatic: Shi repeatedly urged him not to disobey the summons. Xiu changed color and said: "This is my own family affair—what concern is it of yours!

sentences.zh: 」師垂涕對曰：「師荷國厚恩，忝參府幕，僚吏之節，敢不盡心。

translations.literal: " Shi answered with tears: "Shi has received the state's deep grace and is honored to serve in Your Highness's staff—in the duty of a subordinate official, how dare I not give my full heart?
translations.idiomatic: " Shi answered through tears: "I have received the state's deep favor and am honored to serve in Your Highness's staff; as a subordinate officer, how could I fail to give my whole heart?

sentences.zh: 但比年以來，國家多故，秦孝王寢疾，奄至薨殂，庶人二十年太子，相次淪廢。

translations.literal: Yet in recent years the state has seen many troubles: Prince Xiaowang of Qin fell ill and suddenly died; the Crown Prince of twenty years was reduced to commoner status in succession—all cast down.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in recent years the state has suffered many blows: Prince Xiaowang of Qin fell ill and died suddenly; the crown prince of twenty years' standing was in turn deposed and reduced to commoner rank.

sentences.zh: 聖上之情，何以堪處！

translations.literal: The holy sovereign's feelings—how can they bear such blows!
translations.idiomatic: How can the holy sovereign's heart endure any more of this!

sentences.zh: 而有敕追王，已淹時月，今乃遷延未去，百姓不識王心，儻生異議，內外疑駭，發雷霆之詔，降一介之使，王何以自明？

translations.literal: Yet an edict summoning Your Highness has already lingered for months, and now you delay and do not depart—the people cannot read Your Highness's heart; if dissent arises, alarm within and without, and a thunderous decree is issued with a single envoy dispatched, how will Your Highness clear yourself?
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoning Your Highness has already dragged on for months, yet now you linger and will not go—the people cannot read Your Highness's intent; if rumors spread and alarm rises within and without, and a thunderous decree arrives with a single envoy, how will Your Highness prove your innocence?

sentences.zh: 願王自計之。

translations.literal: I urge Your Highness to weigh this for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Highness to consider this carefully.

sentences.zh: 」秀乃從征。

translations.literal: " Xiu then complied and went as summoned.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiu then obeyed and set out for the capital.

sentences.zh: 秀廢之後，益州官屬多相連坐，師以此獲免。

translations.literal: After Xiu was deposed, many Yizhou officials were implicated by association; Shi escaped punishment on this account.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiu was deposed, many officials in Yizhou were punished by association; Shi was spared on that account.

sentences.zh: 後加儀同三司。

translations.literal: Later he was granted the honorific Grand Master with Pomp equaling a third-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was granted the honorary title of Grand Master with Pomp equaling a third-rank office.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，拜大理少卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, Shi was appointed Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Shi was appointed Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 帝在顯仁宮，敕宮外衛士不得輒離所守。

translations.literal: The Emperor was at Xianren Palace and ordered that palace guards outside must not leave their posts at will.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was at Xianren Palace and decreed that the outer palace guards must not leave their posts without permission.

sentences.zh: 有一主帥，私令衛士出外，帝付大理繩之。

translations.literal: One chief guard privately ordered guards outside to leave; the Emperor handed him over to the Ministry of Justice for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: One chief guard privately ordered the outer guards to leave their posts; the Emperor handed him over to the Ministry of Justice for punishment.

sentences.zh: 師據律奏徒，帝令斬之，師奏曰：「此人罪誠難恕，若陛下初便殺之，自可不關文墨。

translations.literal: Shi, citing the law, memorialized exile; the Emperor ordered execution. Shi memorialized: "This man's crime is truly hard to forgive—but if Your Majesty had killed him at first, that would not have involved the written code.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, citing the statute, recommended penal servitude; the Emperor ordered execution. Shi memorialized: "This man's offense is indeed hard to pardon—but if Your Majesty had killed him at once, that would not have touched the written law.

sentences.zh: 既付有司，義歸恆典，脫宿衛近侍者更有此犯，將何以加之？

translations.literal: Now that he has been handed to the responsible office, the principle returns to the standing statutes—if those who guard the night watch or attend close at hand commit the same offense again, how will you punish them?
translations.idiomatic: Now that the case has been handed to the proper office, justice must follow the regular code—if those on night watch or in close attendance commit the same offense again, what penalty will you apply?

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor then relented.

sentences.zh: 轉刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Punishments Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Punishments Bureau.

sentences.zh: 師居職強明，有口辯，而無廉平之稱。

translations.literal: In office Shi was forceful and clear, eloquent in debate, but he did not win repute for integrity and fairness.
translations.idiomatic: In office Shi was forceful and sharp, skilled in argument, but he won no reputation for integrity and impartiality.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒官。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in office.

sentences.zh: 有子昆玉。

translations.literal: He had a son named Kunyu.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Kunyu.

sentences.zh: 郎茂郎茂，字蔚之，恆山新市人也。

translations.literal: Lang Mao—Lang Mao, courtesy name Weizhi, was a native of Xinshi in Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Mao, courtesy name Weizhi, was a native of Xinshi in Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 父基，齊潁川太守。

translations.literal: His father Ji was governor of Yingchuan in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji served as governor of Yingchuan under Qi.

sentences.zh: 茂少敏慧，七歲誦《騷》、《雅》，日千餘言。

translations.literal: Mao was quick and clever as a youth; at seven he could recite the Songs of Chu and the Classic of Poetry, more than a thousand words daily.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was bright and quick as a boy; at seven he could recite from the Songs of Chu and the Classic of Poetry, more than a thousand characters a day.

sentences.zh: 十五師事國子博士河間權會，受《詩》、《易》、《三禮》及玄象、刑名之學。

translations.literal: At fifteen he studied under National University Erudite Quan Hui of Hejian, learning the Classic of Poetry, the Classic of Changes, the Three Rites, as well as astronomy and the science of punishment and names.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he studied under Quan Hui, erudite of the National University from Hejian, mastering the Classic of Poetry, the Classic of Changes, the Three Rites, and also astronomy, law, and legal nomenclature.

sentences.zh: 又就國子助教長樂張率禮受《三傳》群言，至忘寢食。

translations.literal: He also studied under Zhang Shuaili, assistant erudite at the National University from Changle, receiving instruction in the Three Commentaries and diverse learning—so absorbed he forgot sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: He also studied under Zhang Shuaili, assistant erudite of the National University from Changle, taking the Three Commentaries and a wide range of learning, until he forgot to sleep or eat.

sentences.zh: 家人恐茂成病，恆節其燈燭。

translations.literal: His family feared Mao would fall ill and always rationed his lamp and candles.
translations.idiomatic: His family feared he would ruin his health and constantly limited his lamp oil and candles.

sentences.zh: 及長，稱為學者，頗解屬文。

translations.literal: When grown, he was acclaimed as a scholar and was quite skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he was acclaimed as a scholar and was quite adept at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 年十九，丁父憂，居喪過禮。

translations.literal: At nineteen he mourned his father's death and observed mourning beyond the prescribed rites.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he entered mourning for his father and observed the rites of bereavement beyond what custom required.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，解褐司空府行參軍。

translations.literal: He served Qi, first taking office as Acting Staff Officer in the Office of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service under Qi, beginning as acting staff officer in the Office of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 會陳使傅縡來聘，令茂接對之。

translations.literal: When the Chen envoy Fu Zan came on a diplomatic mission, Mao was ordered to receive and respond to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen envoy Fu Zan came on a diplomatic visit, Mao was assigned to receive and reply to him.

sentences.zh: 後奉詔于秘書省刊定載籍。

translations.literal: Later, by imperial order he collated and corrected historical records at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later, by imperial order, he collated and corrected historical texts at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷保城令，有能名，百姓為立《清德頌》。

translations.literal: He was promoted to magistrate of Baocheng, where he won renown for competence; the people erected for him an "Eulogy of Pure Virtue."
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Baocheng, where he won a reputation for ability; the people composed an Eulogy of Pure Virtue in his honor.

sentences.zh: 及周武平齊，上柱國王誼薦之，授陳州戶曹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, the Upper Pillar of State Wang Yi recommended him; he was appointed registrar of the household bureau in Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, the Upper Pillar of State Wang Yi recommended him, and he was appointed registrar of the household bureau in Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 屬高祖為亳州總管，見而悅之，命掌書記。

translations.literal: When Gaozu served as grand commander of Bozhou, he met Mao, was pleased with him, and appointed him chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaozu served as grand commander of Bozhou, he met Mao, was pleased with him, and appointed him chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 時周武帝為《象經》，高祖從容謂茂曰：「人主之所為也，感天地，動鬼神，而《象經》多糾法，將何以致治？

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wu of Zhou composed the Classic of Images; Gaozu said casually to Mao: "What the ruler does moves Heaven and Earth and stirs spirits—yet the Classic of Images is full of binding rules; how is one to govern well?
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Wu of Zhou had composed the Classic of Images; the Gaozu said casually to Mao: "A ruler's actions should move Heaven and Earth and stir the spirits—yet the Classic of Images is full of restrictive rules; how can one govern well by it?

sentences.zh: 」茂竊歎曰：「此言豈常人所及也！

translations.literal: " Mao sighed privately: "These words—how could an ordinary man reach them!
translations.idiomatic: " Mao sighed to himself: "Words like these—how could an ordinary man utter them!

sentences.zh: 」乃陰自結納，高祖亦親禮之。

translations.literal: " He then secretly attached himself to Gaozu, who also treated him with personal esteem.
translations.idiomatic: " He then quietly attached himself to the Gaozu, who in turn treated him with personal respect.

sentences.zh: 後還家為州主薄。

translations.literal: Later he returned home and served as chief clerk of his province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned home and served as chief clerk of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，以書召之，言及疇昔，甚歡。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became chancellor, he summoned Mao by letter; speaking of old times, they were greatly delighted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaozu became chancellor, he summoned Mao by letter; recalling old times together, they were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 授衛州司錄，有能名。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief clerk of Weizhou, again winning renown for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief clerk of Weizhou, again winning a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 尋除衛國令。

translations.literal: Soon he was made magistrate of Weiguo.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed magistrate of Weiguo.

sentences.zh: 時有系囚二百，茂親自究審數日，釋免者百餘人。

translations.literal: At the time there were two hundred prisoners in custody; Mao personally examined cases for several days and released more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: At the time two hundred men were held in custody; Mao personally reviewed the cases for several days and released more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 歷年辭訟，不詣州省。

translations.literal: For years, lawsuits did not reach the provincial or central offices.
translations.idiomatic: For years lawsuits never reached the provincial or central authorities.

sentences.zh: 魏州刺史元暉謂茂曰：「長史言衛國民不敢申訴者，畏明府耳。

translations.literal: The governor of Weizhou, Yuan Hui, said to Mao: "The chief clerk says the people of Weiguo dare not lodge complaints because they fear the magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hui, governor of Weizhou, said to Mao: "The chief clerk says the people of Weiguo dare not bring suits because they fear you, magistrate.

sentences.zh: 」茂進曰：「民猶水也，法令為堤防。

translations.literal: " Mao responded: "The people are like water; laws and ordinances are the dikes.
translations.idiomatic: " Mao replied: "The people are like water, and laws and ordinances are the dikes.

sentences.zh: 堤防不固，必致奔突，苟無決溢，使君何患哉？

translations.literal: If the dikes are not secure, overflow is inevitable—but if there is no breach, what worry has the governor?
translations.idiomatic: If the dikes are weak, overflow is sure to follow—but if there is no breach, what has the governor to fear?

sentences.zh: 」暉無以應之。

translations.literal: " Hui had no reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Hui had nothing to say in reply.

sentences.zh: 有民張元預，與從父弟思蘭不睦。

translations.literal: There was a commoner, Zhang Yuanyu, who was on bad terms with his father's younger cousin's son Silan.
translations.idiomatic: Among the people was Zhang Yuanyu, who was estranged from his cousin Silan.

sentences.zh: 丞尉請加嚴法，茂曰：「元預兄弟，本相憎疾，又坐得罪，彌益其忿，非化民之意也。

translations.literal: The assistant magistrate and county captain asked to impose strict punishment. Mao said: "The Yuanyu brothers inherently loathe each other; to punish them further would only deepen their rancor—this is not the spirit of transforming the people.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant magistrate and the county captain asked that strict punishment be applied. Mao said: "Yuanyu and his kinsman already hate each other; to punish them further would only deepen their anger—this is not how one transforms the people.

sentences.zh: 」於是遣縣中耆舊更往敦諭，道路不絕。

translations.literal: " He then sent elders of the county again and again to instruct them; the road was never empty of such envoys.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent the county elders again and again to instruct them, until the road was never without such messengers.

sentences.zh: 元預等各生感悔，詣縣頓首請罪。

translations.literal: Yuanyu and the others were moved to repentance, came to the county seat, and kowtowed to beg forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu and the others were moved to remorse, came to the county seat, and kowtowed to beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 茂曉之以義，遂相親睦，稱為友悌。

translations.literal: Mao enlightened them with principle; thereafter they grew close and harmonious, and were praised as exemplary in brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: Mao enlightened them with right principle; thereafter they became close and harmonious, and were praised as models of brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 茂自延州長史轉太常丞，遷民部侍郎。

translations.literal: Mao moved from chief administrator of Yanzhou to vice director of the Ministry of Rites, then was promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of Population.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was transferred from chief administrator of Yanzhou to vice director of the Ministry of Rites, then promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of Population.

sentences.zh: 時尚書右僕射蘇威立條章，每歲責民間五品不遜。

translations.literal: At that time Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat Su Wei established articles and regulations; every year he required reports from among the people on the five grades of insubordination.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Su Wei, Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat, instituted new regulations requiring annual reports from the populace on the five grades of unfilial and insubordinate conduct.

sentences.zh: 或答者乃雲：「管內無五品之家。

translations.literal: Some who answered would even say: "Within my jurisdiction there are no households of fifth rank."
translations.idiomatic: Some respondents would even reply, "There are no fifth-rank households in my district."

sentences.zh: 」不相應領，類多如此。

translations.literal: " Their answers did not match what was required, and there were many cases like this.
translations.idiomatic: Their answers did not meet the requirement, and such evasions were common.

sentences.zh: 又為餘糧簿，擬有無相贍。

translations.literal: He also created a surplus-grain register, intending mutual support between those who had and those who lacked.
translations.idiomatic: He also instituted a surplus-grain register to arrange mutual aid between households with grain to spare and those without.

sentences.zh: 茂以為繁紆不急，皆奏罷之。

translations.literal: Mao considered these tangled and not urgent, and memorialized to abolish them all.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Mao regarded these measures as needlessly complicated and not pressing, and memorialized to have them all abolished.

sentences.zh: 數歲，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: After several years, he left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 未期，起令視事。

translations.literal: Before the mourning period had expired, he was recalled and ordered to resume his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Before the mourning period was complete, he was recalled to office.

sentences.zh: 又奏身死王事者，子不退田，品官年老不減地，皆發於茂。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that when one died in service to the ruler, the son should not surrender his allotted land, and that when a ranked official grew old his land allotment should not be reduced—all these policies originated with Mao.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that sons of men who died in the ruler's service should not forfeit their inherited land, and that ranked officials should not lose land allotments upon reaching old age—policies that all originated with Mao.

sentences.zh: 茂性明敏，剖決無滯，當時以吏幹見稱。

translations.literal: Mao's nature was bright and keen; in deciding cases he was never delayed, and at the time he was praised for his administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was quick-witted and decisive in adjudication, and was widely praised at the time for his skill as an administrator.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，以本官領大興令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Ren shou reign, he concurrently held his original post and served as magistrate of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Ren shou era he retained his original rank while also serving as magistrate of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，遷雍州司馬，尋轉太常少卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Mao was transferred to be Administrator of Yong Province, and soon after was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Mao was appointed Administrator of Yong Province and soon afterward promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 後二歲，拜尚書左丞，參掌選事。

translations.literal: Two years later, he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and took part in managing appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and shared responsibility for personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 茂工法理，為世所稱。

translations.literal: Mao was skilled in legal principles and was praised by the world.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was expert in legal doctrine and widely admired for it.

sentences.zh: 時工部尚書宇文愷、右翊衛大將軍于仲文競河東銀窟。

translations.literal: At that time Minister of Works Yuwen Kai and General of the Right Wing Guard Yu Zhongwen were competing over the silver mines east of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Minister of Works Yuwen Kai and General of the Right Wing Guard Yu Zhongwen were disputing control of the silver mines east of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 茂奏劾之曰：「臣聞貴賤殊禮，士農異業，所以人知局分，家識廉恥。

translations.literal: Mao memorialized to impeach them, saying: "Your servant has heard that noble and base have different rites, and scholar and farmer different occupations, so that people know their stations and families understand shame.
translations.idiomatic: Mao memorialized to impeach them, writing: "I have heard that the noble and the base observe different rites, and scholars and farmers follow different callings, so that people know their proper stations and households understand shame.

sentences.zh: 宇文愷位望已隆，祿賜優厚，拔葵去織，寂爾無聞，求利下交，曾無愧色。

translations.literal: Yuwen Kai's rank and standing are already lofty, his salary and gifts generous; he should pull up his mallow and leave off weaving, yet he has been utterly silent—seeking profit by consorting with inferiors without the slightest sign of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Kai already enjoys high rank and generous emoluments; he ought to abstain from petty gain, yet he has remained utterly silent while seeking profit through dealings with social inferiors, without a trace of shame.

sentences.zh: 于仲文大將，宿衛近臣，趨侍階庭，朝夕聞道，虞、芮之風，抑而不慕，分銖之利，知而必爭。

translations.literal: Yu Zhongwen is a great general and a close attendant of the inner guard; he attends in the court morning and evening and hears the Way daily, yet he suppresses and does not emulate the spirit of Yu and Rui, and for gains measured in fractions of a coin, knowing them to be trifling, he must still contend.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhongwen is a senior general and a close palace guard who attends the throne daily and hears the Way preached at court, yet he shows no desire to emulate the magnanimity of the lords of Yu and Rui, and will fight over profits no larger than a fraction of a coin.

sentences.zh: 何以貽範庶僚，示民軌物！

translations.literal: How can they set an example for the multitude of officials and show the people the standard of conduct!
translations.idiomatic: How can such men serve as models for the ranks of officials or teach the people proper conduct!

sentences.zh: 若不糾繩，將虧政教。

translations.literal: If they are not investigated and punished, government and instruction will be impaired.
translations.idiomatic: If they are not investigated and punished, governance and moral instruction will suffer.

sentences.zh: 」愷與仲文竟坐得罪。

translations.literal: " Kai and Zhongwen in the end were punished for their offense.
translations.idiomatic: Kai and Zhongwen were ultimately punished for the offense.

sentences.zh: 茂撰《州郡圖經》一百卷奏之，賜帛三百段，以書付秘府。

translations.literal: Mao compiled and submitted the Gazetteer of Prefectures and Commanderies in one hundred juan, and was granted three hundred bolts of silk; the book was deposited in the imperial library.
translations.idiomatic: Mao compiled the Gazetteer of Prefectures and Commanderies in one hundred scrolls and submitted it to the throne, for which he received three hundred bolts of silk; the work was placed in the imperial archives.

sentences.zh: 于時帝每巡幸，王綱已紊，法令多失。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor made frequent inspection tours; the bonds of royal governance were already disordered, and many laws and ordinances had fallen into neglect.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor was touring the realm constantly; imperial governance was in disarray and many laws had fallen into neglect.

sentences.zh: 茂既先朝舊臣，明習世事，然善自謀身，無謇諤之節。

translations.literal: Mao was an old minister of the previous reign and clearly understood worldly affairs, yet he was good at looking after himself and lacked the integrity of forthright remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was a veteran of the previous reign who understood affairs well, but he was adept at self-preservation and lacked the courage for blunt remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 見帝忌刻，不敢措言，唯竊歎而已。

translations.literal: Seeing the emperor's harsh and suspicious nature, he did not dare speak out, and could only sigh in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor's harsh and suspicious temperament, he dared not speak up and could only sigh to himself.

sentences.zh: 以年老，上表乞骸骨，不許。

translations.literal: Because of his advanced age, he submitted a memorial begging to retire, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: On account of his age he submitted a memorial requesting retirement, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 會帝親征遼東，以茂為晉陽宮留守。

translations.literal: When the emperor personally campaigned against Liaodong, Mao was appointed to remain and guard Jinyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor personally marched against Liaodong, Mao was left behind as custodian of Jinyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 其年，恆山贊治王文同與茂有隙，奏茂朋黨，附下罔上。

translations.literal: That year, Wang Wentong, Assistant Administrator of Hengshan, who had a grudge against Mao, memorialized that Mao formed factions and flattered those below while deceiving those above.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wang Wentong, Assistant Administrator of Hengshan, who bore a grudge against Mao, accused him of forming factions and flattering subordinates while deceiving superiors.

sentences.zh: 詔遣納言蘇威、御史大夫裴蘊雜治之。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Remonstrating Minister Su Wei and Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun to investigate jointly.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Remonstrating Minister Su Wei and Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun to conduct a joint investigation.

sentences.zh: 茂素與二人不平，因深文巧詆，成其罪狀。

translations.literal: Mao had long been on bad terms with the two men, who therefore twisted the law with elaborate accusations and established his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Mao had long been at odds with both men, who therefore stretched the law with artful accusations until his guilt was established.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，及其弟司隸別駕楚之皆除名為民，徙且末郡。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged; Mao and his younger brother Chuzhi, Vice Director of the Directorate of Justice, were both stripped of rank and made commoners, and were banished to Qiemo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious; Mao and his younger brother Chuzhi, Vice Director of the Directorate of Justice, were both stripped of office and reduced to commoners, then exiled to Qiemo Commandery.

sentences.zh: 茂怡然受命，不以為憂。

translations.literal: Mao calmly accepted the order and was not troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: Mao accepted the sentence calmly and showed no distress.

sentences.zh: 在途作《登壟賦》以自慰，詞義可觀。

translations.literal: On the road he composed the rhapsody "Climbing the Mound" to console himself; its language and meaning were admirable.
translations.idiomatic: En route he wrote the rhapsody "Climbing the Mound" to comfort himself; its language and sentiment were noteworthy.

sentences.zh: 複附表自陳，帝頗悟。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial explaining himself, and the emperor came to some understanding.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a further memorial in his own defense, and the emperor partly relented.

sentences.zh: 十年，追還京兆，歲餘而卒，時年七十五。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was recalled to the capital region; after more than a year he died, at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was recalled to the capital region; he died a little over a year later, at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 有子知年。

translations.literal: He had a son named Zhinian.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Zhinian.

sentences.zh: 高構高構，字孝基，北海人也。

translations.literal: Gao Gou—Gao Gou, styled Xiaoji, was a native of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gou—Gao Gou, styled Xiaoji, was a native of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 性滑稽，多智，辯給過人，好讀書，工吏事，弱冠，州補主簿。

translations.literal: By nature he was witty and humorous, very clever, and more eloquent than others; he loved reading, was skilled in administrative affairs, and at twenty was appointed chief clerk by the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was witty and quick-witted, unusually eloquent, fond of reading, and skilled in administrative work; at twenty he was appointed chief clerk in his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 仕齊河南王參軍事，曆徐州司馬、蘭陵、平原二郡太守。

translations.literal: He served Qi as an aide on the staff of the Prince of Henan, and successively held the posts of Administrator of Xu Province and Governor of the two commanderies of Lanling and Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he served on the staff of the Prince of Henan, then successively held the posts of Administrator of Xu Province and Governor of Lanling and Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 劉滅後，周武帝以為許州司馬。

translations.literal: After Liu [Zhen] was destroyed, Emperor Wu of Zhou appointed him Administrator of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Liu [Northern Qi] regime, Emperor Wu of Zhou appointed him Administrator of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，轉冀州司馬，甚有能名。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, Gou was transferred to Administrator of Ji Province and gained a great reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, Gou was transferred to Administrator of Ji Province and earned a strong reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 征拜比部侍郎，尋轉民部。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, and soon transferred to the Ministry of Population.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, then soon transferred to the Ministry of Population.

sentences.zh: 時內史侍郎晉平東與兄子長茂爭嫡，尚書省不能斷，朝臣三議不決。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Director of the Secretariat Jin Pingdong and his elder brother's son Changmao disputed the succession as heir; the Secretariat could not decide, and after three rounds of discussion among court officials no conclusion was reached.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Vice Director of the Secretariat Jin Pingdong and his elder brother's son Changmao disputed who was the legitimate heir; the Secretariat could not decide the case, and three rounds of discussion among court officials failed to settle it.

sentences.zh: 構斷而合理，上以為能，召入內殿，勞之曰：「我聞尚書郎上應列宿，觀卿才識，方知古人之言信矣。

translations.literal: Gou decided the case in accordance with reason; the emperor regarded him as capable, summoned him into the inner hall, and commended him, saying: "I have heard that Secretariat gentlemen correspond to the constellations; seeing your talent and judgment, I now know the words of the ancients were true.
translations.idiomatic: Gou rendered a judgment that accorded with principle; impressed, the emperor summoned him to the inner hall and praised him, saying: "They say Secretariat gentlemen correspond to the stars; your talent and judgment show me the ancients spoke truly.

sentences.zh: 嫡庶者，禮教之所重，我讀卿判數遍，詞理愜當，意所不能及。

translations.literal: Legitimate and secondary sons are what ritual teaching holds in highest regard; I have read your decision several times—its wording and reasoning are entirely apt, beyond what I myself could reach.
translations.idiomatic: The distinction between legitimate and secondary sons is what ritual teaching holds most dear; I have read your decision several times, and its reasoning is so apt that I could not have matched it myself.

sentences.zh: 」賜米百石。

translations.literal: " He granted him one hundred shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded him with one hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 由是知名。

translations.literal: From this he became well known.
translations.idiomatic: From this he became widely known.

sentences.zh: 尋遷雍州司馬，以明斷見稱。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Administrator of Yong Province and was praised for clear judgment.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Administrator of Yong Province, where he was praised for clear and decisive judgment.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉吏部侍郎，號為稱職。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Civil Office and was regarded as thoroughly competent in his post.
translations.idiomatic: After a little over a year he was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Civil Office and was considered thoroughly competent.

sentences.zh: 複徙雍州司馬，坐事左轉盩啡令，甚有治名。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Administrator of Yong Province; because of an offense he was demoted to the left and made magistrate of Zhouzhi, where he gained a strong reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to Administrator of Yong Province, then demoted for an offense to magistrate of Zhouzhi, where he nevertheless earned a strong reputation for effective administration.

sentences.zh: 上善之，複拜雍州司馬，又為吏部侍郎，以公事免。

translations.literal: The emperor approved of him, again appointed him Administrator of Yong Province, and once more made him Vice Director of the Ministry of Civil Office; later he was dismissed for an official matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought well of him, reappointed him Administrator of Yong Province and again made him Vice Director of the Ministry of Civil Office, though he was later dismissed over an official matter.

sentences.zh: 煬帝立，召令復位。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, he was summoned and ordered to resume his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Gou was recalled and restored to office.

sentences.zh: 時為吏部者，多以不稱職去官，唯構最有能名，前後典選之官，皆出其下。

translations.literal: At that time many who held the Ministry of Civil Office left their posts for incompetence; only Gou had the greatest reputation for ability, and the officials who had previously managed selection all ranked below him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many heads of the Ministry of Civil Office left office for incompetence; only Gou enjoyed the strongest reputation for ability, and officials who had previously overseen appointments all stood below him.

sentences.zh: 時人以構好劇談，頗謂輕薄，然其內懷方雅，特為吏部尚書牛弘所重。

translations.literal: People at the time, because Gou loved lively talk, largely considered him frivolous, yet inwardly he preserved upright elegance and was especially valued by Minister of Civil Office Niu Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gou loved spirited conversation, many regarded him as somewhat frivolous, yet inwardly he remained upright and refined, and was especially esteemed by Minister of Civil Office Niu Hong.

sentences.zh: 後以老病解職，弘時典選，凡將有所擢用，輒遣人就第問其可不。

translations.literal: Later, because of old age and illness he resigned; when Hong was then managing selection, whenever he was about to promote someone he would send a messenger to Gou's home to ask whether the appointment was suitable.
translations.idiomatic: Later he retired on account of old age and illness; while Niu Hong was managing appointments, whenever he was about to promote someone he would send a messenger to Gou's home to ask whether the choice was sound.

sentences.zh: 河東薛道衡才高當世，每稱構有清鑒，所為文筆，必先以草呈構，而後出之。

translations.literal: Xue Daoheng of Hedong was the most talented man of his age; he always said Gou had clear judgment, and whatever literary work he wrote he would first show in draft to Gou before releasing it.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Daoheng of Hedong, the foremost literary talent of the age, always said Gou had discerning judgment; whatever he wrote he would first show Gou in draft before publishing it.

sentences.zh: 構有所詆訶，道衡未嘗不嗟伏。

translations.literal: Whenever Gou found fault, Daoheng never failed to sigh and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Gou criticized his work, Daoheng invariably sighed and accepted the correction.

sentences.zh: 大業七年，終於家，時年七十二。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daye he died at home, at the age of seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Daye he died at home, at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 所舉杜如晦、房玄齡等，後皆自致公輔，論者稱構有知人之鑒。

translations.literal: Those he recommended, such as Du Ruhui and Fang Xuanling, later all rose to high ministerial rank; commentators said Gou had the discernment to know men.
translations.idiomatic: Those he recommended—including Du Ruhui and Fang Xuanling—later all reached the highest offices; commentators said Gou had a true gift for recognizing talent.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，昌黎豆盧實為黃門侍郎，稱為慎密。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era, Dou Lu Shi of Changli served as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and was praised for discretion and thoroughness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang era, Dou Lu Shi of Changli served as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and was admired for discretion and reliability.

sentences.zh: 河東裴術為右丞，多所糾正。

translations.literal: Pei Shu of Hedong served as Right Vice Director and corrected many abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shu of Hedong served as Right Vice Director and corrected many abuses.

sentences.zh: 河東士燮、平原東方舉、安定皇甫聿道，俱為刑部，並執法平允。

translations.literal: Shi Xie of Hedong, Dongfang Ju of Pingyuan, and Huangfu Yudao of Anding all served in the Ministry of Punishments and were alike fair and even-handed in enforcing the law.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xie of Hedong, Dongfang Ju of Pingyuan, and Huangfu Yudao of Anding all served in the Ministry of Punishments and were equally fair in enforcing the law.

sentences.zh: 弘農劉士龍、清河房山基為考功，河東裴鏡民為兵部，並稱明幹。

translations.literal: Liu Shilong of Hongnong and Fang Shanji of Qinghe served in the Ministry of Merit; Pei Jingmin of Hedong served in the Ministry of War—all were praised as bright and capable.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shilong of Hongnong and Fang Shanji of Qinghe served in the Ministry of Merit, and Pei Jingmin of Hedong in the Ministry of War—all were praised as capable and efficient.

sentences.zh: 京兆韋焜為民曹，屢進讜言。

translations.literal: Wei Kun of Jingzhao served in the Population Bureau and repeatedly submitted forthright remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Kun of Jingzhao served in the Population Bureau and repeatedly offered candid remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 南陽韓則為延州長史，甚有惠政。

translations.literal: Han Ze of Nanyang served as Administrator of Yan Province and had a very benevolent record in office.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ze of Nanyang served as Administrator of Yan Province and governed with notable benevolence.

sentences.zh: 此等事行遺闕，皆有吏幹，為當時所稱。

translations.literal: These men's deeds and omissions are recorded here because they all had administrative ability and were praised in their day.
translations.idiomatic: These men are mentioned here because, though their full careers are not recounted, they all possessed administrative talent and were admired in their time.

sentences.zh: 張虔威張虔威，字元敬，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Qianwei—Zhang Qianwei, styled Yuanjing, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qianwei—Zhang Qianwei, styled Yuanjing, came from Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 父晏之，齊北徐州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yan Zhi was Governor of Northern Xu Province under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan Zhi had been Governor of Northern Xu Province under Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 虔威性聰敏，涉獵群書。

translations.literal: Qianwei was by nature intelligent and quick, and read widely among many books.
translations.idiomatic: Qianwei was intelligent and widely read.

sentences.zh: 其世父嵩之謂人曰：「虔威，吾家千里駒也。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Song Zhi said to others: "Qianwei is the thousand-li colt of our family."
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Song Zhi told others, "Qianwei is the thousand-li steed of our clan."

sentences.zh: 」年十二，州補主簿。

translations.literal: " At twelve he was appointed chief clerk by the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he was appointed chief clerk in his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十八為太尉中兵參軍，後累遷太常丞。

translations.literal: At eighteen he became Central Army Aide in the Ministry of War, and afterward was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he became an aide in the Ministry of War's Central Army section, and was later promoted repeatedly until he reached Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 及齊亡，仕周為宣納中士。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, he served Zhou as Attendant Gentleman for Reception.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Qi he served Northern Zhou as Attendant Gentleman for Reception.

sentences.zh: 高祖得政，引為相府典簽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu took power, he was brought in as Record Keeper in the prince's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu seized power, Qianwei was recruited as record keeper in the prince's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，晉王廣出鎮并州，盛選僚佐，以虔威為刑獄參軍，累遷為屬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, when Prince of Jin Yang Guang went out to command Bing Province, staff members were carefully chosen, and Qianwei was appointed Aide for Criminal Affairs; he was repeatedly promoted until he became a senior staff member.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaihuang, when Prince Yang Guang of Jin went out to take command of Bing Province, Qianwei was selected as an aide for criminal affairs and was promoted repeatedly until he became a senior member of the prince's staff.

sentences.zh: 王甚美其才，與河內張衡俱見禮重，晉邸稱為「二張」焉。

translations.literal: The prince greatly admired his talent; he and Zhang Heng of Henei were both treated with honor, and the prince's household called them "the Two Zhangs."
translations.idiomatic: The prince greatly admired his talent; he and Zhang Heng of Henei were both held in high esteem, and the prince's household called them "the Two Zhangs."

sentences.zh: 及王為太子，遷員外散騎侍郎、太子內舍人。

translations.literal: When the prince became crown prince, Qianwei was transferred to Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant at Court and Palace Secretary to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became crown prince, Qianwei was made Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant at Court and Palace Secretary to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，授內史舍人、儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he was appointed Palace Secretary and granted the rank of Third Order of Honor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Qianwei was appointed Palace Secretary and granted Third Order of Honor.

sentences.zh: 尋以籓邸之舊，加開府。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of his old ties in the prince's household, he was additionally granted the title of General Who Opens a Government Office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, in recognition of his long service in the prince's household, he was additionally granted the title of General Who Opens a Government Office.

sentences.zh: 尋拜謁者大夫，從幸江都，以本官攝江都贊治，稱為幹理。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Master of Ceremonial and accompanied the emperor to Jiangdu; in his original post he concurrently served as Assistant Administrator of Jiangdu and was praised for efficient administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Grand Master of Ceremonial and accompanied the emperor to Jiangdu, where he concurrently served as Assistant Administrator of Jiangdu and was praised for efficient governance.

sentences.zh: 虔威嘗在途見一遺囊，恐其主求失，因令左右負之而行。

translations.literal: Qianwei once on the road saw an abandoned purse; fearing its owner might suffer loss in searching for it, he had his attendants carry it along as they traveled.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the road Qianwei saw an abandoned purse; fearing its owner might lose it while searching, he had his attendants carry it along.

sentences.zh: 後數日，物主來認，悉以付之。

translations.literal: Several days later the owner came to claim it, and he returned everything to him.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later the owner came to claim it, and Qianwei returned everything intact.

sentences.zh: 淮南太守楊綝嘗與十餘人同來謁見，帝問虔威曰：「其首立者為誰？

translations.literal: Yang Shen, Administrator of Huainan, once came with more than ten others to pay an audience; the emperor asked Qianwei: "Who is the one standing at the head?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shen, Administrator of Huainan, once came with more than ten others to pay an audience; the emperor asked Qianwei, "Who is the man at the front?"

sentences.zh: 」虔威下殿就視而答曰：「淮南太守楊綝。

translations.literal: " Qianwei went down from the hall to look closely and answered: "Yang Shen, Administrator of Huainan."
translations.idiomatic: Qianwei descended from the hall to look closely and replied, "Yang Shen, Administrator of Huainan."

sentences.zh: 」帝謂虔威曰：「卿為謁者大夫，而乃不識參見人，何也？

translations.literal: " The emperor said to Qianwei: "You are Grand Master of Ceremonial, yet you do not recognize those who come to audience—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Qianwei, "You are Grand Master of Ceremonial, yet you do not recognize those who come to audience—why is that?"

sentences.zh: 」虔威對曰：「臣非不識楊綝，但慮不審，所以不敢輕對。

translations.literal: " Qianwei replied: "It is not that your servant does not recognize Yang Shen, but I feared I might not be certain, and therefore did not dare answer lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Qianwei replied, "It is not that I fail to recognize Yang Shen, Your Majesty, but I was not fully certain and therefore did not dare answer rashly.

sentences.zh: 石建數馬足，蓋慎之至也。

translations.literal: Shi Jian counted the horses' legs—that is caution carried to the utmost."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian counted the horses' legs—that is caution taken to the utmost."

sentences.zh: 」帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: " The emperor greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly praised him.

sentences.zh: 其廉慎皆此類也。

translations.literal: His integrity and caution were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity and caution were characteristic in this way.

sentences.zh: 于時帝數巡幸，百姓疲敝，虔威因上封事以諫。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor made frequent inspection tours and the common people were worn out; Qianwei therefore submitted a sealed memorial to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor toured constantly and the people were exhausted; Qianwei therefore submitted a sealed memorial of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，自此見疏。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased, and from then on Qianwei was kept at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased, and from then on Qianwei fell from favor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒官。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in office.

sentences.zh: 有子爽，仕至蘭陵令。

translations.literal: He had a son Shuang, who served as magistrate of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Shuang, who served as magistrate of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 虔威弟虔雄，亦有才器。

translations.literal: Qianwei's younger brother Qianxiong also had talent and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Qianwei's younger brother Qianxiong was also a man of talent and ability.

sentences.zh: 秦孝王俊為秦州總管，選為法曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Prince Jun of Qin Xia served as Commander-in-Chief of Qin Province, Qianxiong was selected as Aide for Legal Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jun of Qin Xia served as Commander-in-Chief of Qin Province, Qianxiong was chosen as an aide for legal affairs.

sentences.zh: 王嘗親案囚徒，虔雄誤不持狀，口對百餘人，皆盡事情，同輩莫不嘆服。

translations.literal: The prince once personally examined prisoners; Qianxiong by mistake did not bring the dossiers, yet answered from memory for more than a hundred men, all in full accord with the facts, and none of his colleagues failed to admire him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince once personally reviewed prisoners; Qianxiong forgot to bring the case records, yet answered from memory for more than a hundred men, every detail correct, to the admiration of all his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 後曆壽春、陽城二縣令，俱有治績。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as magistrate of the two counties of Shouchun and Yangcheng, and in both had a record of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He later served successively as magistrate of Shouchun and Yangcheng, governing both counties with distinction.

sentences.zh: 榮毗榮毗，字子諶，北平無終人也。

translations.literal: Rong Pi—Rong Pi, styled Zichen, was a native of Wuzhong in Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Pi—Rong Pi, styled Zichen, was a native of Wuzhong in Beiping.

sentences.zh: 父權，魏兵部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Quan was Minister of War under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quan had been Minister of War under Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 毗少剛鯁有局量，涉獵群言，仕周，釋褐漢王記室，轉內史下士。

translations.literal: Pi from youth was firm, upright, and measured; he read widely among many writings; he served Zhou, and upon first taking office became Recorder to the Prince of Han, then was transferred to Attendant Gentleman in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Pi was firm, upright, and broad-minded; widely read, he entered Zhou service as Recorder to the Prince of Han and was later transferred to Attendant Gentleman in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，累遷殿內監。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era he was repeatedly promoted to Director of Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang era he was promoted repeatedly until he reached Director of Palace Attendants.

sentences.zh: 時以華陰多盜賊，妙選長吏，楊素薦毗為華州長史，世號為能。

translations.literal: At the time because Huayin had many robbers and bandits, [the court] carefully selected a chief administrator; Yang Su recommended Pi as long secretary of Huazhou, and the world called him capable.
translations.idiomatic: Because bandits were rampant in Huayin at the time, the court sought an exceptional local administrator; Yang Su recommended Rong Pi as long secretary of Huazhou, and he was widely regarded as capable.

sentences.zh: 素之田宅，多在華陰，左右放縱，毗以法繩之，無所寬貸。

translations.literal: Yang Su's fields and residences were mostly in Huayin; his retainers were unrestrained, but Pi bound them with the law and granted no leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Most of Yang Su's estates lay in Huayin, where his retainers behaved lawlessly; Pi enforced the law against them without exception.

sentences.zh: 毗因朝集，素謂之曰：「素之舉卿，適以自罰也。

translations.literal: When Pi was at a court assembly, Su said to him: "Su's recommendation of you was precisely to punish himself."
translations.idiomatic: At a provincial assembly Pi attended, Su told him, "Recommending you was my way of punishing myself."

sentences.zh: 」毗答曰：「奉法一心者，但恐累公所舉。

translations.literal: Pi replied: "One who upholds the law with single-minded devotion fears only that he may compromise what you recommended."
translations.idiomatic: Pi answered, "In enforcing the law as I must, I only fear I may discredit your recommendation."

sentences.zh: 」素笑曰：「前者戲耳。

translations.literal: Su smiled and said: "What I said earlier was merely in jest."
translations.idiomatic: Su laughed and said, "I was only joking before."

sentences.zh: 卿之奉法，素之望也。

translations.literal: Your upholding of the law is what Su hoped for.
translations.idiomatic: Your strict adherence to the law is exactly what I wanted."

sentences.zh: 」時晉王在揚州，每令人密覘京師消息。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Jin was in Yangzhou and often sent men secretly to observe news from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Jin was stationed at Yangzhou and frequently sent agents to spy on events in the capital.

sentences.zh: 遣張衡于路次往往置馬坊，以畜牧為辭，實給私人也。

translations.literal: He dispatched Zhang Heng to set up horse pastures here and there along the routes, using livestock raising as a pretext but in fact supplying his private followers.
translations.idiomatic: He had Zhang Heng establish horse farms at intervals along the roads—ostensibly for breeding stock, but in reality to supply his private retinue.

sentences.zh: 州縣莫敢違，毗獨遏絕其事。

translations.literal: The prefectures and counties dared not disobey; Pi alone blocked and stopped the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county officials dared not resist, but Pi alone put a stop to it.

sentences.zh: 上聞而嘉之，賚絹百匹，轉蒲州司馬。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and praised this, bestowing a hundred bolts of silk, and [Pi] was transferred to be marshal of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he commended Pi, rewarded him with a hundred bolts of silk, and appointed him marshal of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒之反也，河東豪傑以城應諒。

translations.literal: When Prince of Han Liang rebelled, the powerful men of Hedong responded to Liang with their cities.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Liang of Han rebelled, local magnates in Hedong surrendered their cities to him.

sentences.zh: 刺史丘和覺，遁歸關中。

translations.literal: The inspector Qiu He realized it and fled back to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Qiu He sensed the danger and fled to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 長史渤海高義明謂毗曰：「河東要害，國之東門，若失之，則為難不細。

translations.literal: The long secretary Gao Yiming of Bohai said to Pi: "Hedong is a strategic point, the eastern gate of the state; if lost, the harm would not be slight."
translations.idiomatic: Long secretary Gao Yiming of Bohai told Pi, "Hedong is a vital stronghold—the empire's eastern gate. Losing it would be no small disaster."

sentences.zh: 城中雖複恟渙，非悉反也。

translations.literal: Although there is again disturbance and disorder in the city, not all are rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The city may be in turmoil again, but not everyone there has rebelled."

sentences.zh: 但收桀黠者十餘人斬之，自當立定耳，」毗然之。

translations.literal: "If you simply seize and behead a dozen or so of the fierce and cunning ones, stability will be restored at once," [Gao] said; Pi agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Just arrest and execute a dozen ringleaders and order will be restored at once." Pi agreed.

sentences.zh: 義明馳馬追和，將與協計。

translations.literal: Yiming galloped to overtake He, intending to confer with him on a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Yiming spurred his horse after Qiu He to consult with him on a course of action.

sentences.zh: 至城西門，為反者所殺，毗亦被執。

translations.literal: When they reached the western gate of the city, [Yiming] was killed by the rebels, and Pi was also seized.
translations.idiomatic: At the city's west gate Yiming was killed by the rebels and Pi was captured as well.

sentences.zh: 及諒平，拜治書侍御史，帝謂之曰：「今日之舉，馬坊之事也。

translations.literal: When Liang was pacified, [Pi] was appointed attendant censor for investigating documents; the emperor said to him: "Today's appointment is because of the horse pasture affair."
translations.idiomatic: After Liang's rebellion was suppressed, Pi was made investigating censor. The emperor told him, "This promotion owes to your stand on the horse farms."

sentences.zh: 無改汝心。

translations.literal: Do not change your heart.
translations.idiomatic: Do not change your resolve."

sentences.zh: 」帝亦敬之。

translations.literal: The emperor also respected him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held him in esteem as well.

sentences.zh: 毗在朝侃然正色，為百僚所憚。

translations.literal: Pi in court was forthright and stern in bearing, and the hundred officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: In court Pi was stern and unyielding, and all officials stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 後以母憂去職，歲餘，起令視事，尋卒官。

translations.literal: Later on mourning for his mother he left office; after more than a year he was recalled to resume duty, and soon died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He later resigned to mourn his mother; recalled after a year, he resumed duty and soon died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: [He was] posthumously granted Vice Director of the Court of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made vice director of the Court of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 毗兄建緒，性甚亮直，兼有學業。

translations.literal: Pi's elder brother Jianxu had a very bright and upright nature and also possessed learning.
translations.idiomatic: Pi's elder brother Jianxu was notably upright and learned.

sentences.zh: 仕周為載師下大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He served Zhou as junior grand master of the chariot masters and commissioner with the third rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he served as junior grand master of the chariot masters and commissioner of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 及平齊之始，留鎮鄴城，因著《齊紀》三十卷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the pacification of Qi he was left to garrison Ye city, and thereupon wrote Records of Qi in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was first conquered he was left to garrison Ye, where he wrote the Records of Qi in thirty chapters.

sentences.zh: 建緒與高祖有舊，及為丞相，加位開府，拜息州剌史。

translations.literal: Jianxu had old ties with Emperor Gaozu; when [Gaozu] became chancellor, [Jianxu] was given the status of opening a government office and appointed inspector of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jianxu had long known Emperor Gaozu; when Gaozu became chancellor he granted Jianxu opening-a-fu rank and made him inspector of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 將之官，時高祖陰有禪代之計，因謂建緒曰：「且躊躇，當共取富貴。

translations.literal: As he was about to take up his post, at the time Gaozu secretly had a plan to receive the abdication, and therefore said to Jianxu: "Wait a while—we shall together obtain wealth and eminence."
translations.idiomatic: As Jianxu was about to leave for his post, Gaozu—already scheming to seize the throne—told him, "Hold on; we shall rise to power together."

sentences.zh: 」建緒自以周之大夫，因義形於色曰：「明公此旨，非僕所聞。

translations.literal: Jianxu regarded himself as a minister of Zhou; righteousness showed in his expression as he said: "Your lordship's meaning—this is not something I have heard."
translations.idiomatic: Counting himself a Zhou minister, Jianxu colored with indignation and said, "My lord, such talk I have never heard before."

sentences.zh: 」高祖不悅，建緒遂行。

translations.literal: Gaozu was displeased, and Jianxu thereupon departed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu took offense, and Jianxu went on his way.

sentences.zh: 開皇初來朝，上謂之曰：「卿亦悔不？

translations.literal: In the early Kaihuang era he came to court; the emperor said to him: "Do you also regret it?"
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang reign he came to court. The emperor asked him, "Do you regret it now?"

sentences.zh: 」建緒稽首曰：「臣位非徐廣，情類楊彪。

translations.literal: Jianxu prostrated himself and said: "Your servant's position is not that of Xu Guang; his sentiment is like that of Yang Biao."
translations.idiomatic: Jianxu kowtowed and replied, "I am no Xu Guang in rank, but my loyalty is that of Yang Biao."

sentences.zh: 」上笑曰：「朕雖不解書語，亦知卿此言不遜也。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "Although We do not understand the language of books, We also know that your words are not deferential."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed. "Though I am no scholar, I can tell that was hardly a humble answer."

sentences.zh: 」曆始、洪二州刺史，俱有能名。

translations.literal: He served successively as inspector of Shizhou and Hongzhou, both with a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as inspector of Shizhou and Hongzhou, earning a name for ability in both posts.

sentences.zh: 陸知命陸知命，字仲通，吳郡富春人也。

translations.literal: Lu Zhiming—Lu Zhiming, style name Zhongtong, was a native of Fuchun in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhiming, styled Zhongtong, was from Fuchun in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 父敖，陳散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His father Ao was Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry under Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ao had been attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry under the Chen dynasty.

sentences.zh: 知命性好學，通識大體，以貞介自持，釋褐陳始興王行參軍，後曆太學博士、南獄正。

translations.literal: Zhiming by nature loved learning, understood the broad principles, and maintained himself with integrity; he first took office as acting adjutant to the Prince of Shixing of Chen, and later served successively as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and director of the southern prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiming loved scholarship, grasped affairs at a high level, and held himself to strict integrity. He entered service as adjutant to Chen's Prince of Shixing, then served as imperial academy erudite and warden of the southern prison.

sentences.zh: 及陳滅，歸於家，會高智慧等作亂于江左，晉王廣鎮江都，以其三吳之望，召令諷諭反者。

translations.literal: When Chen was destroyed he returned home; it happened that Gao Zhihui and others rebelled in the Jiangzuo region; Prince Jin Guang was stationed at Jiangdu and, because [Zhiming] was esteemed in the Three Wu region, summoned him to admonish and persuade the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell he retired home. When Gao Zhihui and others rose in rebellion in the lower Yangzi, Prince Jin Guang at Jiangdu summoned him—renowned in the Jiangnan region—to win over the rebels by persuasion.

sentences.zh: 知命說下賊十七城，得其渠帥陳正緒、蕭思行等三百餘人，以功拜儀同三司，賜以田宅，複用其弟恪為汧陽令。

translations.literal: Zhiming persuaded seventeen rebel cities to submit, capturing their chieftains Chen Zhengxu, Xiao Sixing, and more than three hundred others; for his merit he was appointed Commissioner with the Third Rank Insignia, granted fields and residence, and his younger brother Ke was again employed as magistrate of Qianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiming persuaded seventeen rebel-held cities to surrender and captured more than three hundred ringleaders including Chen Zhengxu and Xiao Sixing. For this he was made commissioner of the third rank and given land and a house; his younger brother Ke was appointed magistrate of Qianyang.

sentences.zh: 知命以恪非百里才，上表陳讓，朝廷許之。

translations.literal: Zhiming considered Ke not talented for a hundred-li district, submitted a memorial declining [the appointment for him], and the court approved.
translations.idiomatic: Believing Ke unfit for county magistracy, Zhiming memorialized to decline the appointment on his brother's behalf, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 時見天下一統，知命勸高祖都洛陽，因上《太平頌》以諷焉。

translations.literal: Seeing that the realm was unified, Zhiming urged Gaozu to make Luoyang the capital, and thereupon submitted "Ode to Great Peace" to admonish him thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the empire unified, Zhiming urged Gaozu to move the capital to Luoyang and submitted an "Ode to Great Peace" to press the point.

sentences.zh: 文多不載。

translations.literal: The text is largely not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the text is not preserved.

sentences.zh: 數年不得調，詣朝堂上表，請使高麗，曰：「臣聞聖人當扆，物色芻蕘，匹夫奔踶，或陳狂瞽。

translations.literal: For several years he received no new appointment; he went to the court hall and submitted a memorial requesting to be sent to Goguryeo, saying: "Your servant has heard that when a sage faces the throne screen, he seeks out humble folk and firewood gatherers; common men may rush forward and sometimes present mad blindness."
translations.idiomatic: After several years without a new appointment he went to the court and memorialized asking to be sent as envoy to Goguryeo: "I have heard that a sage on the throne seeks counsel even from woodcutters in the lanes, and that common men pressing forward may sometimes speak rash folly."

sentences.zh: 伏願暫輟旒纊，覽臣所謁。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly wishes that you would briefly set aside the pearl tassel and cotton padding and peruse what your servant presents.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to pause your state duties and give ear to what I submit."

sentences.zh: 昔軒轅馭曆，既緩夙沙之誅，虞舜握圖，猶稽有苗之伐，陛下當百代之末，膺千載之期，四海廓清，三邊底定，唯高麗小豎，狼顧燕垂。

translations.literal: Formerly Xuanyuan held the calendar and still deferred the punishment of Susha; Yu Shun grasped the chart yet still delayed the campaign against the Miao; Your Majesty stands at the end of the hundred generations and receives the appointment of a thousand years—within the four seas is pure clarity, the three frontiers are settled—only the petty brat of Goguryeo, like a wolf looking back at Yan's border.
translations.idiomatic: Even Huangdi, when he took the throne, delayed punishing Susha; even Emperor Shun, though he held the mandate, postponed the Miao campaign. Your Majesty stands at the turn of ages with all under heaven pacified and the frontiers secure—only Goguryeo's upstart ruler glares wolfishly from across the northeastern marches."

sentences.zh: 王度含弘，每懷遵養者，良由惡殺好生，欲諭之以德也。

translations.literal: The royal measure is inclusive and broad; each time he cherishes following and nurturing, it is truly because he hates killing and loves life, wishing to instruct them with virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's gracious forbearance and preference for conciliation stem from a genuine hatred of killing and love of life—you wish to win them over through virtue."

sentences.zh: 臣請以一節，宣示皇風，使彼君臣面縛闕下。

translations.literal: Your servant requests with one bamboo tally to proclaim the imperial influence, so that their lord and ministers may come bound before the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Allow me to go as your envoy, proclaim the imperial virtue, and bring their ruler and ministers bound before the palace gates."

sentences.zh: 」書奏，天子異之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Son of Heaven was struck by it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed when the memorial reached him.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，授普寧鎮將。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed general of Puning garrison.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he was made garrison general at Puning.

sentences.zh: 人或言其正直者，由是待詔于御史台。

translations.literal: Some people spoke of his uprightness; because of this he was retained as awaiting edicts at the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: When word of his integrity reached court, he was retained at the Censorate awaiting imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，拜治書侍御史，侃然正色，為百僚所憚，帝甚敬之，後坐事免。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, [Zhiming] was appointed attendant censor for investigating documents; forthright and stern in bearing, he was feared by the hundred officials, and the emperor greatly respected him; later he was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne Zhiming became investigating censor. Stern and fearless, he awed the officials and earned the emperor's respect, though he was later dismissed after an incident.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，複職。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was reinstated.

sentences.zh: 時齊王暕頗驕縱，昵小人，知命奏劾之。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Qi Kan was quite arrogant and unrestrained and was intimate with petty men; Zhiming memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kan of Qi was then flagrantly arrogant and kept company with worthless men; Zhiming impeached him by memorial.

sentences.zh: 暕竟得罪，百僚震栗。

translations.literal: Kan in the end was punished; the hundred officials trembled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was eventually punished, and officials throughout court were shaken.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，為東暆道受降使者，卒于師，時年六十七。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he served as surrender-receiving envoy on the eastern coast route and died in the army at age sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign he served as surrender envoy on the eastern route and died in camp at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈御史大夫。

translations.literal: [He was] posthumously granted Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 房彥謙房彥謙，字孝沖，本清河人也，七世祖諶，仕燕太尉掾，隨慕容氏遷于齊，子孫因家焉。

translations.literal: Fang Yanqian—Fang Yanqian, style name Xiaochong, was originally from Qinghe; his seventh-generation ancestor Chen served as aide to the Grand Commandant of Yan, followed the Murong clan in migrating to Qi, and his descendants made their home there.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yanqian, styled Xiaochong, was originally from Qinghe. His seventh-generation ancestor Chen had served as aide to Yan's grand commandant; following the Murong clan's move to Qi, the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 世為著姓。

translations.literal: For generations they were a prominent clan.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they were a leading clan in the region.

sentences.zh: 高祖法壽，魏青、冀二州刺史，壯武侯。

translations.literal: His ancestor Fashou was inspector of Qing and Ji provinces under Wei, Marquis Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: An ancestor, Fashou, had been joint inspector of Qing and Ji under Wei and held the title Marquis Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖伯祖，齊郡、平原二郡太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Bozu was administrator of Qi and Pingyuan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Bozu had been administrator of Qi and Pingyuan commanderies.

sentences.zh: 祖翼，宋安太守，並世襲爵壯武侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yi was administrator of Song'an; all for generations inherited the title Marquis Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yi was administrator of Song'an; for generations they inherited the title Marquis Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 父熊，釋褐州主簿，行清河、廣川二郡守。

translations.literal: His father Xiong, upon first taking office, was chief clerk of the prefecture and acting administrator of Qinghe and Guangchuan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiong entered service as a prefectural chief clerk and served as acting administrator of Qinghe and Guangchuan.

sentences.zh: 彥謙早孤，不識父，為母兄之所鞠養。

translations.literal: Yanqian was orphaned early, did not know his father, and was raised by his mother's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Yanqian never knew his father and was raised by his maternal elder brother.

sentences.zh: 長兄彥詢，雅有清鑒，以彥謙天性穎悟，每奇之，親教讀書。

translations.literal: His eldest brother Yanxun had refined discernment; because Yanqian was by nature clever and perceptive, [Yanxun] always marveled at him and personally taught him to read.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest brother Yanxun had keen judgment; noting Yanqian's natural brilliance, he took a special interest in the boy and taught him to read himself.

sentences.zh: 年七歲，誦數萬言，為宗黨所異。

translations.literal: At age seven he could recite tens of thousands of words and was regarded as unusual by the clan kin.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he could recite tens of thousands of characters, and kinsmen regarded him as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 十五，出後叔父子貞，事所繼母，有逾本生，子貞哀之，撫養甚厚。

translations.literal: At fifteen he was made heir to his uncle Zizhen; in serving his adoptive mother he exceeded [what he showed] his birth mother; Zizhen pitied him and raised him with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he was adopted by his uncle Zizhen. He cared for his adoptive mother even more devotedly than his own, and Zizhen, moved by his plight, lavished affection on him.

sentences.zh: 後丁所繼母憂，勺飲不入口者五日。

translations.literal: Later when mourning for his adoptive mother, for five days he did not take a spoonful of drink into his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: When his adoptive mother died he mourned so deeply that for five days he took not even a spoonful of food or drink.

sentences.zh: 事伯父樂陵太守豹，竭盡心力，每四時珍果，口弗先嘗。

translations.literal: In serving his uncle Bao, administrator of Leling, he exhausted his heart's strength; whenever seasonal delicacies and fruits [were served], his mouth did not taste them first.
translations.idiomatic: Serving his uncle Bao, administrator of Leling, he gave himself entirely to the task; when seasonal delicacies arrived he never tasted them before his uncle.

sentences.zh: 遇期功之戚，必蔬食終禮，宗從取則焉。

translations.literal: When encountering relatives in the qi and gong degrees of mourning, he invariably ate vegetables until the rites ended; clan members took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: On mourning occasions he ate only plain fare until the rites were complete, and kinsmen looked to him as their example.

sentences.zh: 其後受學于博士尹琳，手不釋卷，遂通涉五經。

translations.literal: Afterward he received instruction from Erudite Yin Lin; his hand never released the scroll, and he thereupon thoroughly covered the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He later studied under erudite Yin Lin, never setting his books aside, until he had mastered the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 解屬文，工草隸，雅有詞辯，風概高人。

translations.literal: He understood composing prose, was skilled at cursive and clerical script, elegantly possessed rhetoric and disputation, and his bearing surpassed ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote well, excelled at cursive and clerical calligraphy, debated with grace, and carried himself above the common run.

sentences.zh: 年十八，屬廣甯王孝珩為齊州刺史，辟為主簿。

translations.literal: At age eighteen, when Prince Guangning Xiaohang was inspector of Qizhou, [Yanqian] was recruited as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen, when Prince Guangning Xiaohang became inspector of Qizhou, he recruited Yanqian as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時禁網疏闊，州郡之職，尤多縱弛，及彥謙在職，清簡守法，州境肅然，莫不敬憚。

translations.literal: At the time the prohibition net was sparse and wide; prefecture and commandery duties were especially lax and slack; when Yanqian took office he was pure, simple, and law-abiding—the commandery territory was orderly, and none did not respect and fear [him].
translations.idiomatic: Laws were loosely enforced and local officials generally negligent, but once Yanqian took office his clean, strict administration brought order to the prefecture and inspired universal respect and fear.

sentences.zh: 及周師入鄴，齊主東奔，以彥謙為齊州治中。

translations.literal: When Zhou armies entered Ye, the Qi ruler fled east; Yanqian was appointed aide-de-camp of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou forces entered Ye and the Qi ruler fled east, Yanqian was made chief aide of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 彥謙痛本朝傾覆，將糾率忠義，潛謀匡輔。

translations.literal: Yanqian grieved his dynasty's overthrow and planned to gather and lead the loyal and righteous, secretly plotting to restore and assist [the state].
translations.idiomatic: Grieved by his dynasty's fall, Yanqian planned to rally loyal men and secretly plot restoration.

sentences.zh: 事不果而止。

translations.literal: The affair did not succeed and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，歸於家。

translations.literal: When Qi perished he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi's fall he retired to his home.

sentences.zh: 周帝遣柱國辛遵為齊州刺史，為賊帥輔帶劍所執。

translations.literal: The Zhou emperor dispatched Pillar of State Xin Zun as inspector of Qizhou; he was seized by the bandit chief Fu Daijian.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor sent pillar of state Xin Zun as inspector of Qizhou, but bandit leader Fu Daijian seized him.

sentences.zh: 彥謙以書諭之，帶劍慚懼。

translations.literal: Yanqian with a letter instructed him; Daijian was ashamed and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqian wrote to admonish him, and Daijian was shamed into submission.

sentences.zh: 送遵還州，諸賊並各歸首。

translations.literal: [He] sent Zun back to the prefecture, and all the bandits each surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Daijian released Xin Zun and returned him to his post; the bandits all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪之後，遂優遊鄉曲，誓無仕心。

translations.literal: After Gaozu received the abdication, [Yanqian] thereupon wandered leisurely in the villages and lanes, vowing to have no mind to serve in office.
