translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the throne Yanqian lived quietly at home, swearing never again to enter official service.

sentences.zh: 開皇七年，刺史韋藝固薦之，不得已而應命。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaihuang, Inspector Wei Yi firmly recommended him; unable to refuse, he accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 7 Inspector Wei Yi repeatedly recommended him, and Yanqian accepted office only under compulsion.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書盧愷一見重之，擢授承奉郎，俄遷監察御史。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Lu Kai upon one meeting greatly valued him, promoted and appointed him Gentleman for Attending Submission, and soon transferred him to supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Lu Kai took an immediate liking to him, appointed him gentleman for attending submission, and soon made him supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 後屬陳平，奉詔安撫泉、括等十州，以銜命稱旨，賜物百段，米百石，衣一襲，奴婢七口。

translations.literal: Later when Chen was pacified, by imperial edict he pacified and reassured ten prefectures including Quan and Kuo; because he fulfilled the commission according to intent, he was granted a hundred bolts of goods, a hundred shi of rice, one suit of clothing, and seven slave servants.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen was conquered he was ordered to pacify ten prefectures including Quan and Kuo; for carrying out the mission successfully he received a hundred bolts of goods, a hundred shi of grain, a suit of clothes, and seven household slaves.

sentences.zh: 遷秦州總管錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be recording secretary under the overall commander of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to recording secretary on the staff of Qinzhou's overall commander.

sentences.zh: 嘗因朝集，時左僕射高熲定考課，彥謙謂熲曰：「書稱三載考績，黜陟幽明，唐、虞以降，代有其法。

translations.literal: Once during an assembly for court audience, when Left Vice Director Gao Bi was establishing merit evaluation, Yanqian said to Bi: "The Classic says 'evaluate merit every three years, demote the obscure and promote the clear'—from Tang and Yu downward, each age has had its method."
translations.idiomatic: At a provincial assembly while left vice director Gao Bi was conducting merit reviews, Yanqian told him, "The classics prescribe triennial performance reviews to separate the worthy from the unworthy—a principle observed since the days of Yao and Shun."

sentences.zh: 黜陟合理，褒貶無虧，便是進必得賢，退皆不肖，如或舛謬，法乃虛設。

translations.literal: If demotion and promotion are reasonable and praise and censure without loss, then advancement necessarily obtains the worthy and retirement all obtain the unworthy; if there are errors, the law is then set up in vain.
translations.idiomatic: When promotions and demotions are sound and praise and blame accurate, advancement brings in the capable and dismissal removes the unfit; any mistake renders the whole system meaningless."

sentences.zh: 比見諸州考校，執見不同，進退多少，參差不類。

translations.literal: Recently I have seen merit evaluation in the prefectures—held views differ, the number of promotions and demotions vary, uneven and not alike.
translations.idiomatic: Recent reviews across the prefectures apply wildly different standards, so the numbers promoted or demoted vary inconsistently."

sentences.zh: 況複愛憎肆意，致乖平坦，清介孤直，未必高名，卑諂巧官，翻居上等，直為真偽混淆，是非瞀亂。

translations.literal: Moreover favorites and hates are indulged at will, causing departure from level fairness; the pure, incorruptible, solitary, and upright do not necessarily receive high marks, while base flatterers and crafty officials instead occupy top ranks—truly authenticity and falsity are mixed, and right and wrong are muddled and chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: Worse, personal favor sways the results: upright men need not rank highly while sycophants and schemers rise to the top, until merit and fraud are indistinguishable and right and wrong utterly confused."

sentences.zh: 宰貴既不精練，斟酌取捨，曾經驅使者，多以蒙識獲成，未曆台省者，皆為不知被退。

translations.literal: The chief nobles are neither proficient nor practiced; in weighing selection and rejection, those who have once served as envoys mostly pass through acquaintance and recognition, while those who have not passed through the secretariat and ministries are all dismissed as unknown.
translations.idiomatic: The ranking officials lack the expertise to judge fairly: those previously known to them pass easily, while worthy men who have never served at court are dismissed as unknown quantities."

sentences.zh: 又四方懸遠，難可詳悉，唯量准人數，半破半成。

translations.literal: Moreover the four directions are distant and far, difficult to know in detail; they only measure according to head count, half failing and half passing.
translations.idiomatic: Remote provinces are hard to assess in detail, so reviewers simply split the difference—roughly half pass and half fail."

sentences.zh: 徒計官員之少多，莫顧善惡之眾寡，欲求允當，其道無由。

translations.literal: They merely count the number of officials as more or less, without regard to the multitude or fewness of good and evil—if one wishes proper appropriateness, there is no way to obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: They count heads rather than weigh virtue and vice, so a fair outcome is impossible."

sentences.zh: 明公鑒達幽微，平心遇物，今所考校，必無阿枉，脫有前件數事，未審何以裁之？

translations.literal: Your lordship perceives what is hidden and subtle, treats things with level heart; the evaluation you now conduct must be without favoritism and distortion—if there are the several matters mentioned above, may I ask how you will decide them?
translations.idiomatic: You, my lord, see clearly and judge impartially, and I am sure your review will be fair; but if these problems I have named arise, how will you resolve them?"

sentences.zh: 唯願遠布耳目，精加採訪，褒秋毫之善，貶纖介之惡，非直有光至治，亦足標獎賢能。

translations.literal: Your servant only wishes that you would broadly deploy eyes and ears, carefully add investigation and inquiry, praise goodness even to an autumn hair's breadth, demean evil even to a fine tip—this would not only bring luster to perfect governance, but also suffice to mark out and reward the worthy and capable.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to seek evidence far and wide, reward the slightest merit and punish the smallest fault—that would honor your governance and encourage worthy men throughout the empire."

sentences.zh: 」詞氣侃然，觀者屬目。

translations.literal: His words and tone were forthright; onlookers fixed their eyes on him.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke with fearless clarity, and all present watched intently.

sentences.zh: 熲為之動容，深見嗟賞。

translations.literal: Bi was moved in bearing by this and deeply showed admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was visibly moved and deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 因曆問河西、隴右官人景行，彥謙對之如響，熲顧謂諸州總管、刺史曰：「與公言，不如獨與秦州考使語。

translations.literal: Thereupon he successively asked about the conduct of officials in Hexi and Longyou; Yanqian answered like an echo. Bi turned and said to the overall commanders and inspectors of the prefectures: "Talking with you gentlemen is not as good as speaking alone with the evaluation envoy from Qinzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Bi then quizzed him on officials throughout Hexi and Longyou; Yanqian answered instantly. Bi turned to the regional commanders and prefects and said, "Talking with all of you is nothing compared with speaking with Qinzhou's review commissioner alone."

sentences.zh: 」後數日，熲言於上，上弗能用。

translations.literal: Several days later Bi spoke to the emperor; the emperor could not employ [the suggestion].
translations.idiomatic: Days later Bi reported to the emperor, but the emperor did not act on it.

sentences.zh: 以秩滿，遷長葛令，甚有惠化，百姓號為慈父。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was transferred to be magistrate of Changge; he had great benevolent transformation, and the common people called him compassionate father.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he became magistrate of Changge, governed with notable kindness, and the people called him their compassionate father.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，上令持節使者巡行州縣，察長吏能不，以彥謙為天下第一，超授鄀州司馬。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era the emperor ordered commissioners bearing the staff to tour prefectures and counties, inspecting whether the chief officials were capable or not; Yanqian was ranked first under heaven and was specially promoted to be marshal of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou reign the emperor sent commissioners to tour the provinces and assess local administrators; Yanqian was ranked the finest in the empire and was promoted to marshal of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 吏民號哭相謂曰：「房明府今去，吾屬何用生為！

translations.literal: Officials and commoners wept aloud and said to one another: "Magistrate Fang is leaving now — of what use is our living!"
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people wept and said to one another, "Now that Magistrate Fang is going, what reason do we have to go on living!"

sentences.zh: 」其後百姓思之，立碑頌德。

translations.literal: Thereafter the common people missed him and erected a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the people missed him, they raised a monument to celebrate his goodness.

sentences.zh: 鄀州久無刺史，州務皆歸彥謙，名有異政。

translations.literal: Ezhou had long lacked a governor; all prefectural affairs fell to Yanqian, and his reputation was for outstanding administration.
translations.idiomatic: Ezhou had gone without a governor for a long time, so Yanqian handled all its affairs and became known for exceptional governance.

sentences.zh: 內史侍郎薛道衡，一代文宗，位望清顯，所與交結，皆海內名賢。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Xue Daoxheng was a literary master of his generation, of lofty rank and eminence; all with whom he formed friendships were celebrated worthies throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Xue Daoxheng was the leading literary figure of his age, a man of high standing and distinction whose circle included the most eminent scholars in the empire.

sentences.zh: 重彥謙為人，深加友敬，及兼襄州總管，辭翰往來，交錯道路。

translations.literal: He highly valued Yanqian's character and treated him with deep friendship and respect; when he also served as Grand Commandant of Xiangzhou, letters flowed back and forth between them, crowding the roads.
translations.idiomatic: He held Yanqian in the highest regard and honored him as a close friend; when he later doubled as grand commandant of Xiangzhou, their correspondence filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，道衡轉牧番州，路經彥謙所，留連數日，屑涕而別。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Daoxheng was transferred to govern Fanzhou; passing Yanqian's place, he lingered for several days and parted with tears.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yang took the throne, Daoxheng was reassigned to Fanzhou; on his way he stopped at Yanqian's home, stayed several days, and left in tears.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎張衡，亦與彥謙相善。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Zhang Heng was also on good terms with Yanqian.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Zhang Heng was another of Yanqian's close friends.

sentences.zh: 于時帝營東都，窮極侈麗，天下失望。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was building the Eastern Capital, pushing extravagance to the utmost, and all under Heaven lost hope.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then building the Eastern Capital with boundless luxury, and the empire lost faith in him.

sentences.zh: 又漢王構逆，罹罪者多，彥謙見衡當途而不能匡救，以書諭之曰：

translations.literal: Moreover the Prince of Han rebelled and many suffered punishment; Yanqian saw that Heng held power at court yet could not rescue the wronged, and wrote to admonish him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Han rose in rebellion and many were punished, Yanqian saw that Zhang Heng held influence at court but could not intervene; he wrote to counsel him, saying:

sentences.zh: 竊聞賞者所以勸善，刑者所以懲惡，故疏賤之人，有善必賞，尊貴之戚，犯惡必刑，未有罰則避親，賞則遺賤者也。

translations.literal: I have heard that rewards exist to encourage good and punishments to chastise evil; therefore for the lowly and humble, if there is good it must be rewarded, and for the noble and honored, if evil is done punishment must be imposed — never has there been one who in punishing avoided kin and in rewarding abandoned the lowly.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that rewards are meant to encourage virtue and punishments to restrain evil. The humble, when they do good, must be rewarded; the highborn, when they do wrong, must be punished. Never yet has a state punished while sparing the powerful and rewarded while neglecting the lowly.

sentences.zh: 今諸州刺史，受委宰牧，善惡之間，上達本朝，懾憚憲章，不敢怠慢。

translations.literal: Now the provincial governors receive commission to shepherd the people; between good and evil their reports reach the central court, and in awe of the law they dare not be negligent.
translations.idiomatic: Today's governors are entrusted to rule the people. Good and evil among them should reach the throne, and in fear of the law they ought not to slacken.

sentences.zh: 國家祗承靈命，作民父母，刑賞曲直，升聞於天，夤畏照臨，亦宜謹肅。

translations.literal: The state reverently receives the divine mandate and acts as parent to the people; the right and wrong of punishments and rewards ascend to Heaven — in reverent fear of divine oversight, one ought also to be strict and solemn.
translations.idiomatic: The state reverently bears Heaven's mandate and serves as parent to the people. Whether punishments and rewards are just is heard in Heaven; under that watchful gaze one should be all the more careful and grave.

sentences.zh: 故文王雲：「我其夙夜，畏天之威。

translations.literal: Therefore King Wen said: "I rise early and retire late, in awe of Heaven's majesty."
translations.idiomatic: King Wen said, "I rise early and lie down late, in awe of Heaven's power."

sentences.zh: 」以此而論，雖州國有殊，高下懸邈，然憂民慎法，其理一也。

translations.literal: Judged by this, though provinces and states differ and rank and distance are far apart, yet caring for the people and being careful in law — the principle is one.
translations.idiomatic: By this reasoning, though provinces differ and ranks stand far apart, the duty to care for the people and uphold the law is the same everywhere.

sentences.zh: 至如并州畔逆，須有甄明。

translations.literal: As for the rebellion at Bingzhou, there must be careful discrimination.
translations.idiomatic: The rebellion at Bingzhou above all requires careful judgment.

sentences.zh: 若楊諒實以詔命不通，慮宗社危逼，徵兵聚眾，非為干紀，則當原其本情，議其刑罰，上副聖主友于之意，下曉愚民疑惑之心；

translations.literal: If Yang Liang truly because imperial edicts did not reach him, fearing danger to the state altars, raised troops and gathered crowds not to violate the norms, then one should consider his original intent and discuss his punishment — matching the sage lord's brotherly intent above and clarifying the foolish people's doubts below;
translations.idiomatic: If Yang Liang truly raised troops because orders never reached him and he feared for the altars of state, not to overturn the law, then his original motive should be weighed and his sentence adjusted — honoring the emperor's brotherly feeling above and clearing the confusion of the common people below;

sentences.zh: 若審知內外無虞，嗣後纂統，而好亂樂禍，妄有覬覦，則管、蔡之誅，當在於諒，同惡相濟，無所逃罪，梟懸孥戮，國有常刑。

translations.literal: If one truly knows that inside and outside were secure and succession was settled, yet he loved chaos and rejoiced in calamity and rashly harbored ambition, then the punishment of Guan and Cai should fall on Liang; those who aided evil cannot escape guilt — hanging heads and destroying families are the state's fixed punishments.
translations.idiomatic: But if it is clear that the realm was secure and the succession assured, and he yet delighted in disorder and nursed unlawful ambition, then he deserves the fate of Guan and Cai; accomplices must not escape, and decapitation and the punishment of kin are the law of the land.

sentences.zh: 其間乃有情非協同，力不自固，或被擁逼，淪陷凶威，遂使籍沒流移，恐為冤濫。

translations.literal: Among them there were some whose hearts were not in accord and whose strength was not their own, or who were coerced and fell under fierce power, so that property was confiscated and they were exiled — I fear this may be wrongful excess.
translations.idiomatic: Among those caught up in it were men whose hearts were never truly with the rebels, who lacked strength of their own, or who were driven by force into submission — yet their estates were seized and they were banished. That may well be unjust excess.

sentences.zh: 恢恢天網，豈其然乎？

translations.literal: The vast net of Heaven — could it really be so?
translations.idiomatic: Can Heaven's far-reaching net truly work this way?

sentences.zh: 罪疑從輕，斯義安在？

translations.literal: When guilt is doubtful, lean toward leniency — where does that principle stand?
translations.idiomatic: When guilt is uncertain, the law favors mercy — where has that principle gone?

sentences.zh: 昔叔向置鬻獄之死，晉國所嘉，釋之斷犯蹕之刑，漢文稱善。

translations.literal: Formerly Shu Xiang had the bribery judge put to death and Jin praised it; Zhang Shizhi refused the capital offense of blocking the imperial procession and Emperor Wen of Han commended him.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Shu Xiang executed a corrupt judge and Jin honored him for it; Zhang Shizhi blocked the harsh sentence for treading on the imperial road and Emperor Wen of Han praised his judgment.

sentences.zh: 羊舌甯不愛弟，廷尉非苟違君，但以執法無私，不容輕重。

translations.literal: Yangshe Ning did not spare his brother; the Minister of Justice did not casually disobey his lord — they simply enforced the law without partiality and did not allow leniency or severity by favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yangshe Ning did not favor his brother, and the Minister of Justice did not lightly defy his sovereign — they upheld the law without private bias and would not bend it for kin or rank.

sentences.zh: 且聖人大寶，是曰神器，苟非天命，不可妄得。

translations.literal: Moreover the great treasure of the sage is called the divine vessel; if it is not Heaven's mandate, it cannot be rashly obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The supreme prize of the sage-king is called the divine vessel; without Heaven's mandate it cannot be seized at will.

sentences.zh: 故蚩尤、項籍之驍勇，伊尹、霍光之權勢，李老、孔丘之才智，呂望、孫武之兵術，吳、楚連磐石之據，產、祿承母后之基，不應曆運之兆，終無帝王之位。

translations.literal: Therefore the valor of Chiyou and Xiang Yu, the power of Yi Yin and Huo Guang, the wisdom of Laozi and Confucius, the military art of Lü Wang and Sun Wu, the linked strongholds of Wu and Chu, the base that Chan and Lu received from the empress dowager — none matched the omens of the destined age, and in the end none gained the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Chiyou and Xiang Yu were peerless warriors; Yi Yin and Huo Guang wielded supreme power; Laozi and Confucius possessed surpassing wisdom; Lü Wang and Sun Wu mastered the art of war; Wu and Chu held territories like bedrock; Chan and Lu rested on the empress dowager's foundation — yet none possessed the signs of the destined age, and none in the end won the throne.

sentences.zh: 況乎蕞爾一隅，蜂扇蟻聚，楊諒之愚鄙，群小之凶慝，而欲憑陵畿甸，覬幸非望者哉！

translations.literal: How much less this tiny corner, bees swarming and ants gathering — Yang Liang's folly and baseness, the wickedness of petty men — yet wishing to threaten the capital and harbor illegitimate hopes!
translations.idiomatic: How much less can a petty corner of the realm, a swarm of bees and ants, the dullness of Yang Liang and the villainy of his hangers-on, hope to threaten the capital and grasp at the throne!

sentences.zh: 開闢以降，書契雲及，帝皇之跡，可得而詳。

translations.literal: Since the opening of the age, written records extend, and the traces of emperors and kings can be examined in detail.
translations.idiomatic: From the beginning of history to the age of writing, the deeds of emperors and kings can be traced in full.

sentences.zh: 自非積德累仁，豐功厚利，孰能道洽幽顯，義感靈祇！

translations.literal: Unless one accumulates virtue and benevolence, abundant merit and thick benefits — who could make the Way penetrate hidden and manifest realms and move the spirits!
translations.idiomatic: Without accumulated virtue and benevolence, great merit and lasting benefit, who could harmonize the seen and unseen worlds and move Heaven itself?

sentences.zh: 是以古之哲王，昧旦丕顯，履冰在念，禦朽競懷。

translations.literal: Therefore the wise kings of antiquity rose before dawn making virtue bright, treading on ice in thought, repairing decay competing in mind.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the sage rulers of old rose before dawn to make their virtue shine, walked as if on thin ice, and strove as if mending a leaking roof.

sentences.zh: 逮叔世驕荒，曾無戒懼，肆於民上，聘嗜奔欲，不可具載，請略陳之。

translations.literal: Until decadent ages of arrogance and dissipation, never cautious or fearful, indulging above the people, greedy and rushing after desires — it cannot all be recorded; allow me briefly to set forth.
translations.idiomatic: Then came decadent ages of pride and excess, without caution or fear, lording it over the people and chasing every appetite — the list is endless; let me mention only a few.

sentences.zh: 襄者齊、陳二國，並居大位，自謂與天地合德，日月齊明，罔念憂虞，不恤刑政。

translations.literal: Recently Qi and Chen, two states, both held the great position; they deemed themselves united in virtue with Heaven, sun and moon equally bright, not thinking of worry, not caring about punishments and governance.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago Northern Qi and Chen both sat on the throne, believing themselves the equal of Heaven and earth, bright as sun and moon, heedless of danger and indifferent to law and government.

sentences.zh: 近臣懷寵，稱善而隱惡，史官曲筆，掩瑕而錄美。

translations.literal: Close ministers cherished favor, praising good and concealing evil; historians twisted their pens, covering flaws and recording beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Favored courtiers praised what was good and hid what was evil; historians bent their pens, glossing over faults and recording only merit.

sentences.zh: 是以民庶呼嗟，終閉塞於視聽，公卿虛譽，日敷陳於左右。

translations.literal: Therefore the common people sighed, ultimately blocked from the ruler's ears and eyes; officials offered empty praise daily laid before his left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The people groaned in misery yet never reached the ruler's ears; officials daily filled his presence with hollow flattery.

sentences.zh: 法網嚴密，刑辟日多，徭役煩興，老幼疲苦。

translations.literal: The legal net was strict and dense, punishments daily multiplied, corvée labor was frequently imposed, and old and young were exhausted in suffering.
translations.idiomatic: The law grew ever tighter, punishments multiplied, corvée burdens mounted, and young and old alike were worn down.

sentences.zh: 昔鄭有子產，齊有晏嬰，楚有叔敖，晉有士會。

translations.literal: In the past Zheng had Zichan, Qi had Yan Ying, Chu had Shu'ao, and Jin had Shi Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng once had Zichan, Qi had Yan Ying, Chu had Shu'ao, and Jin had Shi Hui.

sentences.zh: 凡此小國，尚足名臣，齊、陳之疆，豈無良佐？

translations.literal: All these small states still had famous ministers — could the territories of Qi and Chen lack good assistants?
translations.idiomatic: Even these small states produced great ministers — could Qi and Chen truly have lacked able men?

sentences.zh: 但以執政壅蔽，懷私徇軀，忘國憂家，外同內忌。

translations.literal: But because those in power were obstructive, cherishing private interest and sacrificing themselves, forgetting state and family, outwardly united yet inwardly jealous.
translations.idiomatic: But those in power blocked the truth, served private ends at the state's expense, forgot their duty to ruler and family, and were united in appearance yet jealous at heart.

sentences.zh: 設有正直之士，才堪幹持，於己非宜，即加擯壓；

translations.literal: Should there be an upright man capable in administration, if unsuitable to themselves they would suppress him;
translations.idiomatic: If an upright man of real ability appeared and did not suit them, they crushed him;

sentences.zh: 倘遇諂佞之輩，行多穢匿，于我有益，遂蒙薦舉。

translations.literal: If they encountered flatterers with many hidden vices, if beneficial to themselves they would recommend them.
translations.idiomatic: if they met sycophants steeped in corruption who served their interests, they promoted them.

sentences.zh: 以此求賢，何從而至！

translations.literal: Seeking worthies by this — how could they arrive!
translations.idiomatic: With such methods, how could worthy men ever be found!

sentences.zh: 夫賢材者，非尚膂力，豈系文華，唯須正身負載，確乎不動。

translations.literal: Worthy talent does not value physical strength, nor depends on literary ornament — one need only bear the load with an upright body, firmly unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: True talent is not a matter of brute strength or elegant prose; what matters is to stand upright and bear the weight without wavering.

sentences.zh: 譬棟之處屋，如骨之在身，所謂棟樑骨鯁之材也。

translations.literal: Like ridgepoles in a house, like bones in the body — these are what are called pillar and backbone materials.
translations.idiomatic: Like the beams of a house or the bones of a body — such are the men called pillars and backbones of the state.

sentences.zh: 齊、陳不任骨鯁，信近讒諛，天高聽卑，監其淫僻，故總收神器，歸我大隋。

translations.literal: Qi and Chen did not employ backbones, trusted slander and flattery close by; Heaven is high but hears what is below, watched their licentious excess, and therefore altogether gathered the divine vessel to our great Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and Chen would not use such backbone men and instead trusted slanderers at their side. Heaven, though high, hears what lies below; seeing their depravity, it entrusted the divine vessel to our great Sui.

sentences.zh: 向使二國祗敬上玄，惠恤鰥寡，委任方直，斥遠浮華，卑菲為心，惻隱為務，河朔強富，江湖險隔，各保其業，民不思亂，泰山之固，弗可動也。

translations.literal: If the two states had revered the Supreme, benefited widows and orphans, entrusted the upright, expelled the flashy, taken lowly humility as heart and compassion as task — the north of the river strong and rich, rivers and lakes perilously separated, each keeping their enterprise, people not thinking of disorder — Mount Tai's solidity could not be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Had those two states honored Heaven, cared for the widow and orphan, entrusted the upright, driven away the frivolous, made humility their heart and compassion their work — with the north strong and rich and the south protected by rivers and lakes, each secure in its place and the people untroubled by rebellion — not even Mount Tai could have been shaken.

sentences.zh: 然而寢臥積薪，宴安鴆毒，遂使禾黍生廟，霧露沾衣，吊影撫心，何嗟及矣！

translations.literal: Yet sleeping atop piled kindling, feasting in ease as arsenic poison, they made millet grow in temples, mist and dew soak clothes; mourning one's shadow and clutching the heart — what use lamenting now!
translations.idiomatic: Instead they slept on piled kindling and drank ease like poison, until millet sprouted in ancestral halls and dew soaked the mourner's robes. To clutch one's heart in solitude — what good is regret then!

sentences.zh: 故詩雲：「殷之未喪師，克配上帝。

translations.literal: Therefore the Odes say: "Before Yin had not lost the army, able to match the Supreme Lord."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "Before Yin had yet lost its armies, it could match the Lord on High."

sentences.zh: 宜鑒於殷，駿命不易。

translations.literal: One ought to take Yin as mirror; the great mandate is not easy.
translations.idiomatic: "Take Yin as your mirror; the great mandate is not easily kept."

sentences.zh: 」萬機之事，何者不須熟慮哉！

translations.literal: In the myriad affairs of state — which does not require thorough consideration!
translations.idiomatic: Among the countless duties of government — which does not demand deep reflection!

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇帝望雲就日，仁孝夙彰，錫社分珪，大成規矩。

translations.literal: Humbly — the Emperor looked to clouds and approached the sun; benevolence and filial piety were long manifest; fief and jade tablets were granted; great completion of norms and measure.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, like the people turning to sun and cloud, has long shown benevolence and filial piety, received fief and jade regalia, and fulfilled the rites of rule.

sentences.zh: 及總統淮海，盛德日新，當璧之符，遐邇僉屬。

translations.literal: When presiding over Huaihai, flourishing virtue was daily renewed; the token of destiny to hold the jade — all near and far belonged to it.
translations.idiomatic: When you governed the Huaihai region your virtue grew daily brighter, and the mandate to rule was acknowledged far and near.

sentences.zh: 贊曆甫爾，寬仁已布，率土蒼生，翹足而喜。

translations.literal: Just having ascended the throne, leniency and benevolence were already spread; all within the realm rejoiced with upturned feet.
translations.idiomatic: Barely had you taken the throne when mercy and kindness were proclaimed, and the people everywhere waited eagerly in joy.

sentences.zh: 并州之亂，變起倉卒，職由楊諒詭惑，詿誤吏民，非有構怨本朝，棄德從賊者也。

translations.literal: The disorder at Bingzhou arose in haste; it was caused by Yang Liang's deception misleading officials and people — not those who bore grudges against the dynasty and abandoned virtue to follow rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The trouble at Bingzhou erupted suddenly because Yang Liang deceived officials and people — not because they hated the dynasty and chose rebellion over loyalty.

sentences.zh: 而有司將帥，稱其願反，非止誣陷良善，亦恐大點皇猷。

translations.literal: Yet responsible officials and generals call them willing rebels — not only slandering the good, but also perhaps greatly staining the imperial design.
translations.idiomatic: Yet officials and commanders call them eager rebels — slandering the innocent and, I fear, deeply tarnishing your imperial purpose.

sentences.zh: 足下宿當重寄，早預心膂，粵自籓邸，柱石見知。

translations.literal: You have long borne heavy trust, early participated as heart and sinew; from the princely residence you were known as pillar and stone.
translations.idiomatic: You have long carried great responsibility and were trusted from the start as the emperor's right hand; even in the princely household you were seen as a pillar of the realm.

sentences.zh: 方當書名竹帛，傳芳萬古，稷、契、伊、呂，彼獨何人？

translations.literal: About to have name written on bamboo and silk, fragrance transmitted ten thousand ages — Ji, Qi, Yi, Lü — who are they alone?
translations.idiomatic: You are poised to have your name recorded for ten thousand generations — are Ji, Qi, Yi, and Lü the only great ministers in history?

sentences.zh: 既屬明時，須存謇諤，立當世之大誡，作將來之憲範。

translations.literal: Being in an enlightened age, one must preserve forthright criticism, establish great admonition for the present age, and make a model for future generations.
translations.idiomatic: In an age such as this you must speak frankly, set a great warning for the present, and become a standard for those who come after.

sentences.zh: 豈容曲順人主，以愛虧刑，又使脅從之徒，橫貽罪譴？

translations.literal: How can one bend to please the ruler, letting affection impair punishments, and also make those coerced suffer undeserved blame?
translations.idiomatic: How can you bend to please the throne, soften justice out of favor, and let those who were forced along suffer unjust punishment?

sentences.zh: 忝蒙眷遇，輒寫微誠，野人愚瞽，不知忌諱。

translations.literal: Humbly receiving your gracious favor, I rashly set down my sincere thoughts — a rustic's blindness, not knowing taboos.
translations.idiomatic: Having received your kindness, I venture these sincere words — the blindness of a country man who knows no restraint.

sentences.zh: 衡得書歎息，而不敢奏聞。

translations.literal: Heng received the letter and sighed, but did not dare report it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng read the letter and sighed, but did not dare present it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 彥謙知王綱不振，遂去官隱居不仕，將結構蒙山之下，以求其志。

translations.literal: Yanqian knew the imperial norms were in disorder; he left office, lived in seclusion without serving, and planned to build under Mount Meng to fulfill his will.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the imperial order was failing, Yanqian resigned, withdrew from office, and planned to build a home beneath Mount Meng to live out his ideals.

sentences.zh: 會置司隸官，盛選天下知名之士。

translations.literal: At that time the post of Metropolitan Supervisor was established, and famous scholars throughout the realm were greatly selected.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the court created the office of metropolitan supervisor and sought out the most distinguished men in the empire.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以彥謙公方宿著，時望所歸，征授司隸刺史。

translations.literal: The court, because Yanqian's fairness and rectitude were long renowned and public expectation rested on him, summoned and appointed him Metropolitan Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yanqian's integrity and long-standing reputation made him the man the public looked to, the court summoned him and made him metropolitan supervisor.

sentences.zh: 彥謙亦慨然有澄清天下之志，凡所薦舉，皆人倫表式。

translations.literal: Yanqian also stirred with resolve to clarify all under Heaven; all he recommended were models of human conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqian took up the post with a passion to cleanse the realm; every man he recommended was a model of character.

sentences.zh: 其有彈射，當之者曾無怨言。

translations.literal: Whomever he impeached — those targeted never had complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Those he impeached never bore him resentment.

sentences.zh: 司隸別駕劉灹，陵上侮下，訐以為直，刺史憚之，皆為之拜。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Assistant Liu Zha, overbearing upward and insulting downward, called slander uprightness; supervisors feared him, and all bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Assistant Liu Zha bullied his superiors and abused his subordinates, treating abuse as honesty; other supervisors feared him and bowed in his presence.

sentences.zh: 唯彥謙執志不撓，亢禮長揖，有識嘉之。

translations.literal: Only Yanqian held to his will unmoved, with high ceremony giving a long bow; those with insight praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yanqian stood firm, greeting him with a formal bow instead of a full prostration — men of judgment applauded him.

sentences.zh: 灹亦不敢為恨。

translations.literal: Zha also did not dare hold resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Even Liu Zha did not dare resent it.

sentences.zh: 大業九年，從駕渡遼，監扶餘道軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daye, he followed the emperor crossing the Liao, supervising the army on the Fuyu route.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Daye he accompanied the emperor on the Liaodong campaign as supervisor of the Fuyu-route army.

sentences.zh: 其後隋政漸亂，朝廷靡然，莫不變節。

translations.literal: Afterward Sui governance gradually fell into disorder; the court was listless, and none failed to change their principles.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Sui rule sank into chaos; the court lost its bearings, and nearly everyone abandoned his principles.

sentences.zh: 彥謙直道守常，介然孤立，頗為執政者之所嫉，出為涇陽令。

translations.literal: Yanqian, upright in the Way and constant in conduct, stood alone and isolated, much envied by those in power; he was sent out as magistrate of Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqian held to the straight path and lived by his old standards, alone and apart; the men in power resented him and had him transferred to be magistrate of Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，終於官，時年六十九。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office; he was sixty-nine at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in office, aged sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 彥謙居家，每子侄定省，常為講說督勉之，亹癖不倦。

translations.literal: At home Yanqian, whenever nephews and sons came for daily visits, would explain and exhort them tirelessly without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: At home, whenever his nephews and sons came to pay their respects, Yanqian would instruct and encourage them, tirelessly and without flagging.

sentences.zh: 家有舊業，資產素殷，又前後居官，所得俸祿，皆以周恤親友，家無餘財，車服器用，務存素儉。

translations.literal: The family had old estates and assets always abundant; also salaries from office before and after were all used to aid relatives and friends — the home had no surplus wealth, and carriages, robes, and utensils all kept plain simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: His family held old property and was comfortably well off, yet he spent every salary he earned in office on helping kin and friends. His household kept no surplus, and his carriage, dress, and furnishings were always plain.

sentences.zh: 自少及長，一言一行，未嘗涉私，雖致屢空，怡然自得。

translations.literal: From youth to age, every word and act never involved private affairs; though often empty of means, he was content and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to old age not one word or deed of his was self-serving; though he was often short of money, he remained cheerful and at ease.

sentences.zh: 嘗從容獨笑，顧謂其子玄齡曰：「人皆因祿富，我獨以官貧。

translations.literal: Once he smiled calmly alone, turned and said to his son Xuanling: "People all become rich through salary — I alone am poor through office."
translations.idiomatic: Once he smiled quietly to himself and said to his son Xuanling, "Other men grow rich from their salaries; I alone have grown poor from mine."

sentences.zh: 所遺子孫，在於清白耳。

translations.literal: What I leave descendants lies in integrity alone.
translations.idiomatic: "What I leave my descendants is nothing but a clean name."

sentences.zh: 」所有文筆，恢廓閒雅，有古人之深致。

translations.literal: All his writings were broad, leisurely, and elegant, with the deep flavor of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: His writings were expansive, refined, and elegant, with the depth of the ancients.

sentences.zh: 又善草隸，人有得其尺牘者，皆寶玩之。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in cursive and clerical script; whoever obtained his letters treasured them.
translations.idiomatic: He was also accomplished in cursive and clerical calligraphy; anyone who received one of his letters prized it.

sentences.zh: 太原王邵，北海高構，蓚縣李綱，河東柳彧、薛孺，皆一時知名雅澹之士，彥謙並與為友。

translations.literal: Wang Shao of Taiyuan, Gao Gou of Beihai, Li Gang of Gaoyi, Liu Yu and Xue Ru of Hedong — all famed refined scholars of the time; Yanqian was friends with them all.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao of Taiyuan, Gao Gou of Beihai, Li Gang of Gaoyi, and Liu Yu and Xue Ru of Hedong were all celebrated men of refined character in their day, and Yanqian counted each of them a friend.

sentences.zh: 雖冠蓋成列，而門無雜賓。

translations.literal: Though officials' carriages lined in rows, his gate had no mixed guests.
translations.idiomatic: Though officials' carriages often filled the street before his door, he admitted no unworthy guest.

sentences.zh: 體資文雅，深達政務，有識者咸以遠大許之。

translations.literal: By nature refined and elegant, deeply versed in state affairs — those with insight all promised him a great future.
translations.idiomatic: Refined by nature and deeply versed in government, men of judgment all foresaw a great future for him.

sentences.zh: 初，開皇中，平陳之後，天下一統，論者咸云將致太平。

translations.literal: Initially in the Kaihuang era, after pacifying Chen, the realm was unified; commentators all said it would reach great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang reign, after the conquest of Chen united the empire, many believed a golden age was at hand.

sentences.zh: 彥謙私謂所親趙郡李少通曰：「主上性多忌克，不納諫爭。

translations.literal: Yanqian privately told his intimate Li Shaotong of Zhao commandery: "Our lord by nature is much jealous and harsh, and does not accept remonstrance and dispute."
translations.idiomatic: Yanqian confided to his friend Li Shaotong of Zhao commandery, "The emperor is by nature suspicious and harsh and will not hear honest counsel."

sentences.zh: 太子卑弱，諸王擅威，在朝唯行苛酷之政，未施弘大之體。

translations.literal: The crown prince is weak and lowly; the princes wield authority; at court only harsh cruel governance is practiced — the broad magnanimous substance has not yet been applied.
translations.idiomatic: "The crown prince is feeble, the princes hold too much power, and the court rules by severity alone without the breadth a great empire needs."

sentences.zh: 天下雖安，方憂危亂。

translations.literal: Though the realm is peaceful, I already worry about crisis and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: "The realm may look secure, but I already foresee turmoil."

sentences.zh: 」少通初謂不然，及仁壽、大業之際，其言皆驗。

translations.literal: Shaotong initially thought not so; by the Renshou and Daye eras his words all proved true.
translations.idiomatic: Shaotong at first disagreed, but by the Renshou and Daye reigns every word of Yanqian's had come true.

sentences.zh: 大唐馭宇，追贈徐州都督、臨淄縣公。

translations.literal: When Great Tang held the realm, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prefect of Xuzhou and Duke of Linzi county.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tang took power, he was posthumously made prefect of Xuzhou and Duke of Linzi county.

sentences.zh: 諡曰定。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Ding.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Ding.

sentences.zh: 【論】史臣曰：大廈雲構，非一木之枝；

translations.literal: [Commentary] The historian says: A great hall clouds built — not one tree's branch;
translations.idiomatic: [Commentary] The historian writes: A towering hall is not upheld by a single beam;

sentences.zh: 帝王之功，非一士之略。

translations.literal: A monarch's achievement — not one gentleman's stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: nor is an emperor's achievement the work of one man's wit alone.

sentences.zh: 長短殊用，大小異宜，㮞棁棟樑，莫可棄也。

translations.literal: Long and short have different uses, large and small different suitability; chopping blocks and ridge beams — none may be discarded.
translations.idiomatic: Long and short serve different ends, large and small fit different roles — rough timber and fine beams alike have their place and none should be cast aside.

sentences.zh: 李諤等或文能遵義，或才足幹時，識用顯于當年，故事留於台閣。

translations.literal: Li E and the others — some in writing able to follow righteousness, some in talent sufficient to serve the age; judgment and employment shown in their day, affairs and records left in the halls and archives.
translations.idiomatic: Li E and his fellows — some upheld righteousness in their writing, some had talent enough for their times; their insight and service stood out in their day, and their deeds remain in the records of the court.

sentences.zh: 參之有隋多士，取其開物成務，皆廊廟之榱桷，亦北辰之眾星也。

translations.literal: Considering the many gentlemen of Sui, taking those who opened things and accomplished tasks—all were rafters of the state hall, and also the many stars of the North Star.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying Sui's many worthy men, those who advanced affairs and fulfilled duties were all pillars of the imperial hall, like the host of stars wheeling about the North Star.
